Peace committee member killed, 8 injured in IED blast in Upper South Waziristan market. UPPER SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: One peace committee member was killed while eight others were injured when an improvised explosive device (IED) exploded in Makeen Bazaar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Upper South Waziristan district on Friday, police said. Dera Ismail Khan Regional Police Officer (RPO) Ghulam Mubashir Makin told Dawn that the IED had been attached to a motorcycle by unidentified people. He said the device exploded at around 10:45am, injuring nine people in the busy market. He said three peace committee members — Inayatullah, Sharat Khan and Bangi Khan — were among the nine injured in the blast. The injured peace committee members were taken to the Razmak Hospital for further treatment, while the rest of the injured were taken to a local health facility for medical assistance, he said. Later, Deputy Superintendent of Police Hidayatullah told Dawn that Inayatullah had died after being taken to the hospital. Police also said that the IED blast damaged several shops in the market, destroying merchandise and other items inside. Following the explosion, police cordoned off the area and launched a search operation. Security was tightened in and around the market, while personnel conducted a search for evidence and possible suspects. RPO Makin said police had registered a preliminary report and launched an investigation into the incident. He added that different aspects of the blast were being examined to identify those responsible. The incident comes amid growing concerns over the deteriorating law and order situation in Upper South Waziristan and Lower South Waziristan. Residents have expressed serious concern over the increasing frequency of bomb blasts, targeted killings, kidnappings for ransom, extortion demands against traders and attacks on police and security forces. On Wednesday, armed men had attacked a member of a local peace committee in the Sararogha tehsil of Upper South Waziristan. A police official was martyred in the attack, while the peace committee volunteer sustained injuries.

PM Shehbaz says Makkah defence pact has sent 'message of peace, unity throughout region'. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said that the recent Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan had brought the three countries “closer together” and sent a message of “unity and peace throughout the region”. ​​​​​​​The three countries signed the joint defence agreement at a trilateral summit in Makkah on August 7, pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond. According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), PM Shehbaz made the remarks during a meeting with Saudi Minister for Environment, Water and Agriculture Abdulrahman bin Abdulmohsen Al-Fadley at the Prime Minister’s House in Islamabad. In a statement, the PMO said the premier reaffirmed the “deep-rooted, fraternal ties” between the two countries and conveyed his regards for King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. He underscored that as strategic partners, both Pakistan and the kingdom must now focus their energies towards “deepening economic and agriculture ties to translate their longstanding relationship into a stronger, mutually beneficial trade and investment partnership”. PM Shehbaz also expressed satisfaction at the “constructive engagement” between the two sides, particularly with regard to the export of agricultural products by Pakistan to the kingdom, the statement said. “Both sides also exchanged views on enhancing agricultural productivity in Pakistan, through the use of technology, research and development and more efficient use of water resources,” the statement added. The premier also announced that a delegation of agricultural experts from Pakistan would soon visit Riyadh to carry forward these discussions “with a view to realise the full potential of this partnership”. Meanwhile, the Saudi minister thanked PM Shehbaz for the warm hospitality extended to him and his delegation and reaffirmed the kingdom’s commitment to deepening cooperation with Pakistan across the agriculture, water and food security sectors, the statement concluded. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif during a summit at Al-Safa Palace. The tripartite pact empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them, and reflects their “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”. Pakistan has said that the pact is “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles. On Thursday, Bangladesh Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman said the country would consider joining the pact “positively” if invited by the founding members. CDF Munir meets Saudi minister in Rawalpindi Separately, Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening its partnership with Saudi Arabia, in a meeting with Al-Fadley at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi. The military’s media wing said that the two sides discussed matters of mutual interest, while the CDF highlighted the brotherly relations between the two countries. He reaffirmed the country’s commitment to further strengthening the longstanding strategic partnership. The Saudi minister in turn appreciated Pakistan’s positive role in promoting regional peace and stability, and expressed a desire to enhance cooperation between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, “particularly in the areas of agriculture and environmental sustainability”.

India signs deal with US to buy Javelin anti-tank missile systems. The Indian Army has signed an agreement with the United States to purchase FGM-148 Javelin anti-tank missile systems, the US Embassy in India said on Friday, without disclosing the value of the deal. The medium-range guided missile system, jointly produced by Lockheed Martin and RTX (formerly Raytheon), is a fire-and-forget weapon designed for use against a range of targets, including armoured vehicles, the embassy said, adding that the missile system is already in service with the US Army and Marine Corps, as well as several international customers. US Ambassador Sergio Gor said in a statement that the agreement creates new opportunities for the defence industries of both countries to work together. “This agreement reflects a defence partnership that is growing deeper, more capable, and more consequential,” he was quoted as saying. “We see tremendous potential for future cooperation that strengthens the defence industrial bases of both countries.” New Delhi was not immediately available for comment on the agreement. According to Lockheed , the missile system features an “arched top-attack profile”, with the missile itself flying above its target before striking it from the top, delivering damage where the armour is weakest. The manufacturer dubs it “the world’s premier shoulder-fired anti-armour system”. India is the world’s fifth-largest military spender and the second-largest arms importer after Ukraine, according to data from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. India and the US signed a 10-year defence framework agreement in October. Although ties between the countries have deteriorated in recent months, with Washington imposing high tariffs on Indian goods, punishing New Delhi for purchasing Russian oil and engaging closely with Pakistan, the defence relationship has remained unaffected. In July, New Delhi approved the purchase of a range of military equipment for its defence forces worth $5.46 billion, including missiles, electronic warfare systems and Kamikaze drones. The acquisition was approved “in principle” by the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) comprising top military officers and headed by the defence minister, according to a government statement. The statement said the estimated cost of the deal would be about INR520 billion. It did not specify the period over which the acquisitions would be made or whether the systems approved for purchase would be imported or domestically produced.

Govt withdraws controversial telecom bill, to bring new draft of proposed legislation. ISLAMABAD: The government on Friday withdrew a controversial bill that sought to give telecom licensees sweeping powers to install infrastructure on public and private land , saying it would introduce a new draft of the proposed legislation. The bill, seeking changes to a 1996 act , was originally tabled by Shaza Fatima Khawaja and approved by the National Assembly on June 11 by a majority vote, a day before the presentation of the federal budget 2026-27. It was then taken up in the Senate, where objections were raised about its clauses. On Friday, a motion to withdraw the Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-organization) (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was moved in the upper house of Parliament by Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry on behalf of Information Technology Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja. The motion was passed by the House as the stipulated 90-day period for the bill’s passage was nearing expiry. “Upon expiry of the prescribed period, the bill would have proceeded to a joint sitting of Parliament, the convening of which may not take place in the near future,” the Ministry of Information Technology said in a statement . “In order to avoid delays and expedite the legislative process, the ministry has decided to introduce a fresh bill, ensuring that the legislative process proceeds in a timely and effective manner, while retaining the essence of the proposed legislation,” it said. The bill’s statement of objects and reasons said amendments were needed for “swift and coordinated deployment of telecommunication infrastructure”. Highlighting the government’s rationale, Khawaja said last month that the existing legal framework did not meet the demands of modern technologies such as 5G. Under the now-withdrawn bill, no public authority was to demand any “charges, fees, rent, of any nature whatsoever” for access. If a public authority did not respond within 30 days of a licensee’s request, even after a reminder, approval was to be “deemed to have been granted”. For private land, licensees were to seek approval from owners/tenants by registered mail. No response in 30 days would allow the matter to be referred to the “appropriate government.” For housing societies, cooperative schemes and commercial estates, access was to be deemed approved after 30 days, though owners could impose conditions on timing and manner of work. “Disputes must be settled within 45 days by an officer not below the rank of secretary,” the bill said. It defined “private access” to include individual ownership and collective ownership by housing societies, Defence Housing Authority and cantonments. “Public authority” covered federal and provincial governments and local bodies. The bill also proposed fines of up to Rs50 million on any owner, tenant or entity that obstructed access. The clauses triggered a strong backlash , with critics calling them “draconian” and saying that they violated Article 23 of the Constitution, which protects property rights. The Islamabad Bar Association and digital rights groups warned the law could be used for “forced entry” into private premises. Several lawmakers, from both opposition and treasury benches, also raised concerns, while the PPP flat out refused to support the bill in the Senate. Following public criticism and media reports, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice and constituted a committee headed by Minister for Law and Justice Azam Nazeer Tarar to examine the legislation. Khawaja later clarified that the bill “would not allow anyone to occupy private land”. Officials said the new draft would retain right-of-way provisions for public infrastructure but make prior consent mandatory for private property. Officials said the amendments were aimed at removing right-of-way bottlenecks that have delayed fibre and 5G rollout in Pakistan. They said the nationwide rollout of modern telecommunications services required extensive infrastructure, including fibre-optic networks, telecom towers and both underground and overground installations. The number of fibre-based internet connections has increased from two million to over five million in the past two years, through various policy and technical interventions, and a target has been set to double this in the next three years. Telecom operators had lobbied for the law, citing months-long delays in getting no-objection certificates from cantonments, housing societies and provincial authorities.

Pims fire: Mustafa Kamal says 'no one will be spared', calls for reforming health sector. Minister for National Health Services Regulation and Coordination Mustafa Kamal on Friday vowed that “no one will be spared” while talking about the fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) that claimed the lives of 14 infants, adding that the country’s health sector needed to be reformed. Speaking in the Senate, Kamal said: “No one intends to spare or save anyone. I am saying this on behalf of the prime minister and the entire government that not a single person will be spared”. He said that the tragedy cannot be an “episode lasting merely a few days,” as he called for accountability and for efforts to prevent such incidents in the future. The minister warned against “suppressing the issue” and invited the House to work towards a way forward, agreeing to a proposal seeking the formation of a parliamentary committee comprising opposition members to investigate Wednesday’s incident. “Look at your resources, management and actions and then involve everyone to suggest a way forward,” he said, assuring that the government will support such an approach. “This is a matter of children’s lives, and we are answerable to God for it. The ministry is nothing; we cannot ruin our afterlife for these ministries,” he remarked. At the outset of his address, the minister expressed sorrow at the lives lost in the incident. “There can be no explanation for this. I am holding myself responsible, and I have presented myself to be held accountable.” He called for a holistic approach toward investigating the incident, urging that any committee formed to probe should not be “time-bound and should remain open”. “When you go investigate this incident, you will find so many things associated with it,” he said, pointing to a larger “rot” within the sector. Kamal held that the health sector was not “ideal”. “Four hundred thousand children between the ages of one and five die every year, 1,300 die every day; they are all dying preventable deaths,” he said. He continued: “It is not possible to bring back the infants who died at Pims, but let us look at it as a test from God and prevent the next kid from dying.” Kamal maintained that there was “no point” in making speeches if the government failed to learn from the incident. “Start from me,” Kamal said, offering himself up for accountability. “Sit with us and save the next from dying. I am putting the entire ministry at your disposal; every person will be answerable to you,” he said. He noted that the system was “rotten” and went on to say: “Where do I find a better person after removing an incompetent one?” Kamal said that when the day ended, “1,300 children would have died across the country”. Speaking about the inquiry committee’s report on the incident, which he said would be presented by tonight, Kamal assured the House: “If you don’t trust it, fair enough [..] we will listen to you.” The health minister once again reassured the House that, “No one will be spared, no matter how influential they are”. “We have to come up with a solution, and I am inviting you to guide us and [..] give us a strategic roadmap,” he said. Kamal said that the health ministry would provide all the relevant input and information. “Sit with us and find a way forward on how to prevent the next child from dying due to negligence within the resources that we have. I assure you of its implementation”. However, he added that if matters were to move in that direction, “no MNA should call and ask why a certain doctor was removed”. Calling for “radical reforms” in the health sector, Kamal urged that the Pims fire “can serve as a basis for how we can prevent more children from dying”. The minister further stated that he was “withholding his information” on the fire until the committee’s report. “If you are dissatisfied (with the report), then form a committee, and everyone stands ready to be held accountable”. Concluding his address, Kamal urged that the “issue should be only closed at a point where we can prevent similar incidents in the future”. “I am willing to sit here all night and listen,” he added. The minister, during his address, in response to calls for his resignation, said: “Let the investigation be completed. I have already taken action beyond what they are thinking.” Sherry Rehman calls for accountability; PTI’s Ali Zafar proposes formation of committee The routine business in the Senate was suspended on a motion moved by PPP parliamentary leader in the House Senator Sherry Rehman for a thorough discussion on the Pims fire. Speaking in the Senate, Rehman stressed that the incident raised serious questions of governance, accountability and public safety. “Wherever there is a failure, there must be accountability. Audit and accountability are an integral part of politics. Working for public interest in the Senate is politics. Politics is to work for the good of people, to work for public interest. Politics is all about accountability.“ she stressed. Rehman said her concerns were also rooted in her own experience as a former health minister. “I have served as health minister for six months. I was also given reasons to close the emergency gates, but I did not. Instead, I posted guards there and checked myself. Why are incompetent people who don’t care about basic safety protocols even allowed to continue?” “The executive director of Pims was lying when he said that the emergency gate was not closed. The firefighters and the Capital Development Authority (CDA) have stated that the gate was closed. What is the purpose of an emergency exit? It is supposed to remain open for emergencies,” Rehman questioned. Rehman also pointed to contradictions between the Pims report and the findings of CDA, particularly concerning the hospital’s fire-safety arrangements. “The PIMS report contradicts the CDA’s findings. The CDA has repeatedly stated that the hospital’s fire-safety arrangements are inadequate. Why was no notice taken? The hospital does not even have a fire NOC.” Senator Rehman highlighted the substantial federal funding provided to Pims, and questioned why basic safety standards had not been ensured despite the availability of resources. PTI leader Barrister Ali Zafar proposed the formation of a special committee comprising an equal number of government and opposition members, with an opposition member as its head. He said the committee should examine hospital safety and emergency preparedness and develop comprehensive Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for dealing with foreseeable hazards and emergencies. The committee, he proposed, should also ensure that these SOPs are available, properly implemented and regularly reviewed in every hospital “Let us start with Islamabad,” he said. Zafar further proposed that the committee be empowered to inspect hospitals, call for records, seek explanations from hospital administrations and co-opt medical, fire-safety, engineering, disaster-management and other relevant experts whenever required. He said the administrations of all hospitals should be directed to fully cooperate with the committee and provide all necessary information, records, facilities and assistance required for it to perform its mandate. “This should not be another committee that merely produces a report which sits on a shelf,” he said. According to Zafar, the committee should be focused on identifying failures, correcting them, establishing enforceable safety protocols and ensuring compliance. “We owe this not only to those who lost their lives in this tragedy, but to every patient and every family who will have to depend on our hospitals in the future,” he said. The Senate also passed unanimously a resolution calling for the formation of a special Senate committee to investigate the incident on Friday. It was moved by Senator Rehman. NA passes resolution for inquiry into fire Meanwhile, the National Assembly unanimously approved a resolution, calling for an impartial inquiry into the incident and expressing condolences to the affected families. Through the resolution, a copy of which is available with Dawn , lawmakers expressed “profound grief and sorrow” over the incident and strongly condemned it. They raised alarm at the circumstances surrounding the fire, with the resolution stating that the circumstances were a result of “sheer negligence”. It called upon the government to “take strict action against anyone responsible for negligence or safety lapses in accordance with the law”. Lawmakers also called on the government to ensure that fire safety and emergency preparedness measures were strictly implemented in federal government hospitals, particularly in neonatal and paediatric units, to prevent such incidents in the future. “The House […] extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and prays for strength and fortitude for them in this hour of profound grief,” the resolution added. Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar expressed his condolences and informed the NA about the steps taken by the prime minister. He said that PM Shehbaz had constituted two committees — one headed by Dr Azhar Kiani and the other by former Secretary Shahid Khan. The committee headed by Dr Kiani would provide information on what was required for the improvement of Pims. The minister also asked for concrete suggestions to be made in the House instead of the issue being politicised. Former prime minister and PPP leader Raja Pervez Ashraf said that the nation had a “habit” of forming a committee or a commission on such matters to keep it alive, but eventually forgetting about the incident within a few weeks. “We need to have a change of approach towards hazards and the health sector,” he said. Ashraf criticised that even after days, nobody was clear about the reasons for the accident, calling for a committee of parliamentarians belonging to all parties in the House to investigate the matter and “at least” inquire into the cause of the fire. PTI senior leader Asad Qaiser noted that the fateful incident occurred at the same hospital that the government claimed had the best facilities when it came to the treatment of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan. Last week, Imran had undergone a medical check-up at Pims — rather than Islamabad’s private Shifa International Hospital as per the directions of the Supreme Court — before being shifted back to Adiala jail. Rs5m compensation announced for affected families Earlier in the day, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry announced Rs5 million compensation for each family affected by the fire. Recalling Wednesday’s incident while speaking to the media at Pims, Chaudhry lamented that 14 infants had fallen victim to “someone’s criminal negligence”. He added that the prime minister had constituted an inquiry committee that was expected to present its report today, assuring that all those “on-duty individuals found guilty of negligence will be given exemplary punishment”. The minister said the grief of the affected families could not be compensated for. “Neither can their children be brought back, nor can their grief be reduced,” he added. “But to provide some relief […] the prime minister has announced that Rs5 million will be given to all the affected families.” Chaudhry said he was visiting Pims to hand over a cheque to one of the affected families on behalf of the prime minister, adding that the compensation amount would be deposited in the accounts of the deceased children’s mothers. “This is a small effort to share their sorrow,” he remarked. Responding to a question about demands for DNA tests of the bodies, he said most of the deceased children died in the incident not because they were burnt but because of suffocation due to smoke. “So all of them could be identified,” he said, adding that after birth, infants had tags with their mothers’ names on their arms. “So they were easily identified.” Deadly fire at Pims On Wednesday, 14 babies were killed after a fire erupted at the Mother and Child Healthcare Centre at Pims. According to a Pims statement, the incident was “initially caused by a spark inside the nursery at 06:38am”, and within seconds a massive fire erupted due to oxygen points at each incubator. It said two doctors and two nurses on duty responded immediately and called security staff, who tried twice to enter the nursery before a blast occurred and the ceilings collapsed. But, witnesses said they waited hours for emergency services and were forced to smash windows to reach the affected ward, while some alleged that doors were locked. The hospital and government later disputed claims of delays and locked emergency exits. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has formed a high-level inquiry committee to probe the incident and removed federal Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri. The tragedy has since sparked widespread outrage and calls for accountability, with the National Assembly’s Standing Committee on National Health Services also demanding answers from the Pims administration over possible negligence and safety lapses.

'No oath, no membership': ECP withdraws notification for Senate by-poll on seat won by PTI's Murad Saeed. ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Friday formally withdrew its April 2 notification for the by-election programme for a general Senate seat from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which it had earlier declared vacant following the disqualification of PTI senator-elect Murad Saeed. In a notification, the ECP withdrew the election programme issued under its April 2 notification to “fill one general seat” in the Senate from KP, in pursuance of an order dated Aug 20. The withdrawal came a week after critics accused the ECP of assuming the role of a court by interpreting the Constitution to hold that no lawful vacancy had been created. Senate elections for 11 vacant seats from KP were held on July 21 last year. Saeed was declared a returned candidate for a general seat on July 24, 2025. However, on March 7 this year, Saeed was convicted by Rawalpindi’s Anti-Terrorism Court-I and sentenced to 10 years of imprisonment in the State vs Asim Rehman case, and on March 25, the commission determined that Saeed had been disqualified under Article 63(1)(h) of the Constitution. His seat was accordingly declared vacant. The by-poll was fixed for April 23 in the KP Assembly, but the process was halted after a petition was filed by PML-N MPA Jalal Khan, who argued that no lawful vacancy existed to justify the by-election. No oath, no membership, commission says In its detailed order, the ECP held that a clear constitutional distinction existed between a “returned candidate” and a “Member of Parliament”. “The publication of such notification signifies the conclusion of the electoral process to the extent of declaring a person as the returned candidate. However, such declaration, by itself, does not confer upon the returned candidate the constitutional status of a member of the Majlis-i-Shoora (Parliament),” the order states. Citing Article 255(3), the commission noted: “Where a person is required by the Constitution to make an oath before he enters upon an office, he shall be deemed to have entered upon the office on the day on which he makes the oath.” It further referred to Article 65, which bars a person from sitting or voting “until he has made before the House oath in the form set out in the Third Schedule”. The ECP noted the significance of the deliberate use of the expression “person elected” instead of “Member” in Article 65, saying that it demonstrated that “the Constitution itself recognises a distinction” between a person who had been elected or returned, and a person who had acquired the status of a member. Until the administration of the prescribed oath, a returned candidate remains a person elected to the House and does not attain the constitutional status of a Member,” the order reads. The ECP also interpreted Article 64 and Article 63(1) to mean that resignation or disqualification leading to a vacancy applied only to a person who had already acquired membership. “Therefore, the question of a seat becoming vacant arises only after the constitutional relationship of membership has been established,” it said. On Article 63(1)(h), the commission said clauses (g) and (h) “must be read in conjunction with the expression ‘from being a member’, as these provisions relate to circumstances where an existing member incurs a disqualification affecting his continuance in office”. The order concluded that a person could not be declared to have lost a seat which he had never occupied as a member, nor could a vacancy arise “in respect of a seat where the constitutional status of membership was never acquired”. “The commission is of the considered view that, notwithstanding the conviction of Murad Saeed, he has not yet acquired the status of a Member of Parliament; therefore, no lawful vacancy has arisen in respect of the said seat,” it said, adding that the question of holding a by-election therefore did not arise. Accordingly, the commission accepted the application and withdrew the April 2 election programme. Although the notification to withdraw the election programme after around five months is available on ECP’s official website, the order it was based on is not available.

10 of 12 parties prequalified for Fesco privatisation, K-Electric withdraws. ISLAMABAD: The Privatisation Commission Board on Friday approved the prequalification of 10 out of 12 interested parties (IPs) for the sale of Faisalabad Electric Supply Company (Fesco), after K-Electric (KE) withdrew its papers and a lone Chinese firm failed to demonstrate sufficient interest in the competition. The development came after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed the relevant authorities to adopt a “comprehensive strategy” earlier this month to attract international investors for the privatisation of state-owned power distribution companies (Discos) and complete the restructuring of the Privatisation Commission within one month. Informed sources said KE, the country’s only privatised power utility, had decided to withdraw rather than risk being disqualified due to the non-availability of its financial accounts for the past two years — a key requirement. They said the company would bid for another distribution company (Disco) as part of a consortium with Shahryar Chishti’s AsiaPak Investments, one of KE’s major shareholders. “K-Electric has withdrawn its Expression of Interest (EOI) for Fesco’s privatisation,” a KE spokesperson confirmed when contacted. He added that the decision was taken because the Disco’s audited financial statements were not yet available, pending finalisation of the company’s Multi-Year Tariff (MYT), which was beyond KE’s control. “We remain committed to pursuing opportunities that maximise value for our stakeholders“, he said. On the other hand, Jiang Xi Electric Power Construction of China did not meet the prequalification criteria, as it filed its EOI in Chinese rather than English on the last day of the deadline, despite repeated requests to submit it in English. The board meeting, presided over by Prime Minister’s Adviser on Privatisation and Privatisation Commission Chairman Muhammad Ali, approved all other prospective bidders for the next stage. The board was informed that a total of 12 EOIs had been received for Fesco. After evaluating the submissions against the approved prequalification criteria, the financial adviser recommended 10 IPs for prequalification. Three are from Turkiye — Aktor Elektrik Enerji Yatırımları San ve Tic AŞ, Genvera Enerji AŞ (Celik Group) and Cengiz Enerji Sanayii ve Ticaret AŞ. The remaining seven Pakistani groups are Engro Energy Limited; Sapphire Fibres Limited, Hub Power Holdings, Lucky Cement and Metro Ventures; Shirazi Investments (Pvt) Limited (Atlas Group); Maple Leaf Cement and Kohinoor Textile; the Pakgen Limited Consortium, comprising Nishat Mills, Nishat Power, Nishat Chunian, Lalpir, Pak Elektron Ltd and Kohinoor Energy; and Artistic Milliners (Private) Limited. The prequalified parties will now proceed to the next stage of the transaction in accordance with the approved process, including access to the Virtual Data Room (VDR) for detailed buy-side due diligence. The board also approved the reconstitution of its Audit and Risk, Human Resources, Investment and Legal committees. The commission said the privatisation aims to improve operational efficiency, modernise distribution infrastructure, strengthen customer service, reduce losses and support a more financially sustainable power sector. Over time, these measures will help create the conditions for more competitive electricity distribution and affordable, reliable power for consumers, it added. Fesco is among the three electricity distribution companies in Disco Batch-I privatisation, alongside Gujranwala Electric Power Company ( Gepco ), which attracted 11 EOIs, most of them also in the run for Fesco and Islamabad Electric Supply Company (Iesco). The deadline for submission of EOIs for Iesco is September 7, 2026. The Privatisation Commission said it would ensure an open, transparent and competitive privatisation process, undertaken in the public interest and in support of the federal government’s wider power-sector reform agenda. Earlier this week, the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority notified sweeping guaranteed performance and overall performance standards for all Discos after more than two decades, to ensure compliance even after going into private hands under the ongoing privatisation process. The new Performance Standards (Distribution) Regulations 2026, issued by the regulator after almost two years of consultations with stakeholders, replace the Discos Performance Rules 2005. Under the new standards, utilities will, for the first time, face mandatory consumer compensation, besides heavy fines, if they fail to meet strict deadlines for restoring power after blackouts, replacing faulty meters, addressing voltage fluctuations, providing new connections and other services.

SECP introduces unified framework for 'faster and easier' entry into Pakistan's capital market. ISLAMABAD: The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has introduced a unified digital investor onboarding framework to make entry into Pakistan’s capital market “faster and easier by reducing repetitive verification, simplifying documentation and setting clear timelines for opening investor accounts”. The framework aims particularly to facilitate first-time and digital investors, with ‘Sehl/Sahulat’ accounts to be processed within one working day and normal accounts within two working days, according to an SECP statement issued on Friday. “Applicants will receive tracking IDs, while any deficiencies will be communicated within the prescribed timeframe and reasons for rejection provided in writing,” it stated. The statement said the initiative was part of the SECP’s broader drive to expand retail participation, particularly among young Pakistanis, and increase the country’s capital-market investor base to 2.5 million. “Our focus is to remove entry barriers and use technology to make the investor journey simpler, faster and more accessible,” SECP Chairman Dr Kabir Ahmed Sidhu was quoted as saying. “The objective is to unlock the significant untapped potential of Pakistan’s capital market by broadening participation, particularly among the youth, and building a deeper and more inclusive market,“ he elaborated. The framework standardises onboarding requirements across “securities brokers, asset management companies, insurers and other regulated intermediaries, creating a more consistent investor experience across the regulated financial sector,” the statement said. According to the SECP, the key feature of the framework is the elimination of repetitive customer verification. Where prescribed verification has already been completed by an eligible regulated financial institution or notified third party, intermediaries can rely on that verification instead of requiring investors to repeat the process. “The framework also enables API-based straight-through processing and digital onboarding, including instant UIN issuance and opening of CDC sub-accounts, reducing paperwork and manual intervention,” the SECP said. A few months ago, the government of Pakistan also established the Capital Market Development Fund (CMDF), aimed at promoting financial literacy, expanding financial inclusion and increasing retail investor participation in the capital markets across the country.

PML-N's Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani sworn in as new AJK prime minister. MUZAFFARABAD: PML-N’s Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani was sworn in as Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s prime minister on Friday. Gillani took oath at a televised ceremony, where he expressed gratitude to PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and the party’s senior leadership. Addressing the gathering, the newly elected prime minister said he was thankful for the leadership’s “affection and faith” in him and pledged to uphold that trust. “I am thankful for the leadership and party’s affection and faith in me, and I assure you that even if I have to work day and night, I will uphold this faith,” Gillani said. He urged members of the Legislative Assembly to cooperate with him, stressing that “we must move forward together and build an AJK that is exemplary for the whole world”. “Ours is a small region,” Gillani said, noting that “similar to the rest of the country, AJK also has governance issues and unemployment”. “Why does anyone work in this country? It is so they can put food on the table, give their children a better education and afford to pay hospital bills,” he said, stressing that the three points were “the basis on which his government will move forward”. He emphasised that the youth must be provided employment opportunities. “We have to take all possible efforts to ensure employment for the youth so they may not be led astray and continue on a path to a brighter future”. Gillani stated that the hospitals in the region also needed improvement. “If we address these three things to even a minor extent, many of our tensions will be resolved.” He expressed confidence that the PML-N majority in the legislative assembly will “utilise the experience of senior members and energy of the youth in their ranks”. “I am confident that at the end of our tenure, AJK’s prosperity and development will be used as an example all over Pakistan,” he hoped. Gillani was elected as PM after securing 30 of the 44 votes polled in the assembly earlier in the day. His sole contender was PPP’s Sardar Mukhtar Ahmed Abbasi, who bagged 14 votes in the contest for the top office. The AJK Assembly comprises 53 members, but its present strength is 46 — PML-N’s being 32, including its allies, and PPP’s 14 — because elections to seven seats in Poonch and Sudhnoti districts have yet to be held. However, 44 votes were polled in Friday’s elections as the speaker did not cast his vote and PML-N regional president Shah Ghulam Qadir was not present in the assembly. Qadir, along with former AJK premier Raja Farooq Haider, had previously opposed Gillani’s nomination for the post. However, when assembly proceedings began on Friday, Haider entered the House alongside Gillani. After the votes were counted, Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq announced the result, declaring Gillani as the winner amid clapping and slogans from the galleries. Gillani has succeeded PPP’s Rathore, who was elected as the prime minister in November 2025. Following his election, PM Shehbaz congratulated him and expressed hope that he would “play an effective role in the development of AJK and the welfare of its people”, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported . Citing an official statement, the report said PM Shehbaz credited PML-N leadership and workers’ “hard work” for the party’s victory in AJK. He said the federal government would continue extending all possible support for the development, prosperity and improved living standards of the people of AJK and termed the “continuation of the democratic process in Azad Jammu and Kashmir a welcome development”. PPP’s Yasin appointed opposition leader PPP regional president and senior parliamentarian Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin was appointed Leader of the Opposition in the AJK Legislative Assembly, as per a notification issued by Assembly Secretary Amjed Latif Abbasi. Speaker Farooq approved Yasin’s appointment to the post — the second time he has held the office — under Rule 17(1), sub-rule (3) of the Rules of Procedure, completing the parliamentary setup in the region. He previously served as Leader of the Opposition during the PML-N government from 2016 to 2021 and has been involved in electoral politics since 1990, winning the 1990, 1996, 2011, 2016 and 2021 general elections, while losing the 1991 and 2006 polls. In 2021, he won from two constituencies, while in the recent elections he won one seat and lost the other. In 2001, he fielded his cousin, who also won the election. Additionally, Yasin has held several ministerial positions during PPP governments, including that of senior minister and acting prime minister. In a statement, he said the opposition had a vital role to play in a democratic society and pledged to perform the role responsibly. “Although we have serious reservations about the recent general elections, being a democratic party, we believe in strengthening democratic institutions. We will play our role in further strengthening the AJK Assembly and leave behind healthy democratic traditions,” he said, adding that the opposition would appreciate every good step taken by the government but would “fully oppose every wrong step”. “We will support the government wherever it works for the people and will raise our voice wherever we find anything against their interests,” Yasin added. Gillani’s nomination PML-N’s decision to nominate Gillani was announced by PM Shehbaz at a meeting with four senior PML-N leaders from AJK in Islamabad, late on Wednesday night. The meeting, which took place at the Prime Min­ister’s House, was attended by PML-N AJK President Shah Ghulam Qadir, his predecessor and former AJK premier Raja Farooq Haider, the party’s regional secretary general and asse­mbly speaker, Chaudhry Tariq Farooq, and Deputy Spe­a­ker Ahmed Raza Qadri. The prime minister was accompanied by his aide, Rana Sanaullah, and senior PML-N leader Saad Rafique. Gillani was also invited to the PM House but did not join the meeting, where PM Shehbaz infor­med the visiting leaders that party supremo Nawaz Sharif had decided to nominate Gillani as the party’s candidate for the AJK premiership. The decision, however, triggered a sharp reaction from Qadir and Haider, who reportedly expressed their disagreement and announced that they would not participate in Friday’s election process. However, only Qadir did not participate in the election. Speculation that Gillani could be chosen for the premiership had been rife since he was elected to the assembly on a reserved seat on Aug 24. However, the party’s regional leadership believed that the formula followed in 2016, when Haider was elevated as prime minister, would be repeated this time as well. Following the reaction of the two senior leaders, Sanaullah and Rafique held another meeting with them, but it remained inconclusive, sources told Dawn. In a post-midnight message on X, Qadir assured the “self-respecting people of Azad Kashmir” that he would not compromise on their honour and dignity. “Nawaz Sharif’s slogan of giving respect to the vote will be ensured,” he added. On Thursday afternoon, however, PML-N central information secretary and Punjab senior minister Marriyum Aurangzeb posted on X that PM Shehbaz had finalised Gillani as the party’s candidate and directed him to submit his nomination papers for election as AJK prime minister. AJK polls The elections in the region, originally scheduled for July 27, were divided into phases over security concerns amid unrest in the region. The first phase was held on July 27, the second on Aug 2 and the third on Aug 10. Meanwhile, the third phase was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district. However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation. So far, in the direct elections to 38 constituencies, the PML-N has secured 25 seats while the PPP won 12. The lone MLA-elect of the Awami Dast-o-Bazu party has also joined hands with the PML-N . As for the reserved seats, the PML-N has bagged six and the PPP two. The PPP has alleged widespread rigging and irregularities in the elections.

Nepal flood death toll rises to 579, nearly 2,000 still missing: disaster authority. Nepal’s disaster authority on Friday put the number of people missing after devastating floods at 1,924, two days after the disaster killed at least 579 people in the country. The number of missing includes 517 foreigners, as well as 933 workers on hydropower projects on the rivers where a wall of water powered down on Wednesday morning, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Rescue teams used heavy machinery to dig through mud and debris in Nepalese towns devastated by a flash flood two days ago, as hopes of finding survivors faded and officials worked to reduce the risk of further catastrophic flooding. The flood ripped through villages and valleys, destroying power stations, roads and bridges along a route that links Kathmandu with Lhasa in Tibet and is popular with trekkers and pilgrims. Authorities in Nepal used helicopters to search for survivors and drop emergency supplies to thousands cut off in towns and valleys while emergency services, some using sniffer dogs, recovered dozens of bodies swept down into the plains. Around 320 Indian nationals are still missing in the aftermath of the devastating flash flood, a spokesperson for India’s foreign ministry said, adding that at least 400 were stranded but safe on the Chinese side, while another 96 had crossed into Nepal by land. Rescuer help women to move through a muddy road following flash floods and a mudslide in Trishuli, Nuwakot district, Nepal on August 28, 2026. —Reuters Dibga Tamang was among the last people rescued from the hard-hit town of Rasuwa on Thursday, airlifted along with three others to an army camp in Nuwakot. “All of our people have gone. They are dead,” Tamang said. “I have no one left waiting for me. Everything and everyone is gone. The end.” The sheer amount of water and debris stirred up now risks triggering a further disaster. Nepal’s disaster management authority warned that a lake formed by debris blocking the Bhotekoshi River was rising and at risk of bursting, while on the other side of the border China said that some three million cubic metres of water, the equivalent of about 1,200 Olympic-sized swimming pools, was expected to flow into an already dammed lake over the next three days. There is a high risk the lake could breach, with peak flow expected around September 1, Chinese state media said, citing the water resources ministry. Chinese authorities have mobilised an eight-member engineering team to conduct aerial surveys and 3D modelling of the barrier lake, but accessing it was challenging. “After the glacier collapse created the lake, many isolated cliffs and steep cliffs appeared along it,” one of the engineers, Chen Hanxiao, told CCTV. Chen said the general approach to reducing the lake’s threat is to excavate a drainage channel at a lower point of the dam, but the width and depth of that channel needed calculations based on how fast the water will flow and how quickly the lake will fill. Their next tasks were to monitor the lake and collect data from the lake floor, as well as weather monitoring in the coming days. Nepali Army working to rescue 100 trapped in hydropower tunnel Nepali Army teams searched for more than 100 people trapped inside a hydropower tunnel, as India offered to send a specialised rescue team. India has extensive experience with difficult Himalayan tunnel rescues, including specialised teams of “rat-hole” miners. However, the uncertainty was agonising for families waiting for news. “I have not heard from him since I spoke to him at 7am that day. We have not had any news about them either, if they are being rescued or not,” Sita Adhikari, whose husband was trapped in the hydropower tunnel, told reporters. “We will have hope as long as we have our breath… We need them to be rescued as soon as possible,” she said. Nepali Army helicopters carrying bodies of deceased flood victims land at Trishuli camp in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 28, 2026. — AFP Two army helicopters were sent to the Trishuli 3A hydropower project in the mountainous Rasuwa district. “Our focus is on search and rescue of people… some people are trapped in the tunnel of Trishuli 3A hydropower project,” Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP . “Two helicopters have been dispatched, but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel.” Chinese rescuers reach main site of deadly mudslide Chinese rescuers faced treacherous conditions as they reached the main area wiped out by a deadly mudslide at the Tibet-Nepal border to search for hundreds of missing people, state media reported. Two days after Tibet’s border trade hub of Gyirong was pummelled by a wall of mud and debris, a team of 21 rescuers became the first to reach it in the late afternoon on Friday, state news agency Xinhua said. Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired a meeting of top leaders about rescue operations, as the death toll in Tibet rose to five, with 558 still missing. “There are still many hidden dangers of glaciers, ice lakes and geological disasters in the surrounding area, and rescue is facing great difficulties,” Xinhua reported the leaders as saying. After the mudslide hit on Wednesday, a huge lake formed upstream, raising concerns that it could burst and cause further severe flooding. But risks from that lake are “gradually decreasing”, Chinese state media reported on Friday, adding that rescue operations were “proceeding in an orderly manner”. An excavator in action as rescue workers repair a road leading to Gyirong Port after a mudslide, in Gyirong county, Shigatse, Tibet Autonomous Region, China on August 28, 2026. —Reuters Authorities had earlier paused operations in the worst affected area, citing the risk of renewed flooding due to the lake water beginning to overflow, state broadcaster CCTV said. Later, a CCTV report said water from the lake was “flowing out naturally, with the outflow discharge exceeding the inflow discharge”. “Compared to the high water level in the early morning on August 27, the lake’s water level has dropped by around 10 metres (33 feet), and the risk is gradually decreasing,” it added. It was not immediately clear if the lake was the same as a debris dam that Nepalese authorities warned had burst on Friday. Family members of the missing were being housed in the area by authorities as they waited for news, one woman told AFP . She said she had not been able to reach her relative, a police officer at Gyirong, or his wife, since the disaster happened, and had been told he was missing by his work unit. CCTV said that 499 Chinese nationals and 555 foreigners had been transported out of the disaster zone as of Friday. Rescue workers are using drone-based 3D modelling and thermal imaging detection, as well as manual searches, to locate those still missing, said CCTV . Xi offered Beijing’s help in Nepal’s rescue operations, in a condolence message to the country’s president. “China is willing to actively assist Nepal in its rescue efforts and provide support and aid to the best of its ability,” Xi said according to CCTV . Buildings ‘wiped out like toothpicks’ Around the world, relatives of those missing were desperate for information about their whereabouts. Sneha Sudhir was one of 10 women whose husbands had set out from Nepal on a trek to Tibet’s Mount Kailash when the region was struck by disaster. The men, all from northern Virginia, are among dozens of Americans missing. “Where are they?” Sudhir said tearfully from her home in Chantilly, Virginia, on Thursday. Sudhir said the women were supporting each other and reaching out to officials, politicians and friends and family in the United States and India, hoping for word. “Everybody is taking turns in shedding their tears, wiping it off and getting back to work,” she said. US President Donald Trump said America had offered support to Nepal. Rescued residents react as they meet family members at an army camp following flash floods, in Battar Bazar town of Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 28, 2026. —AFP “Nobody’s ever seen anything quite like that, where very powerful, strong, well-built buildings were wiped out like they were toothpicks. It’s a terrible thing. We are sending aid and we’ve spoken to the leadership and we let them know anything they want, they’ll have.” Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also offered “whatever possible assistance was required” in a phone call with his Nepali counterpart, Balendra Shah, according to a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). He conveyed to Shah that Pakistan was dispatching emergency relief assistance to Nepal in order to help with the relief efforts, the statement said, as well as expressing condolences and “complete solidarity” with the Nepali leadership and people. Ganesh Aryal, the administrator of Chitwan district, said authorities had recovered 103 bodies from the river system in his district, which is about 100 kilometres away in the plains from the worst-hit region of Trishuli. With local hospitals unable to accommodate all the bodies, district authorities were setting up tents and making arrangements for families to claim their dead relatives, he said. Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who visited flood-hit Nuwakot on Thursday, said the situation was still difficult. “All the state agencies are operating at full capacity. Our first priority now is to save the life of each citizen, search and rescue of the missing, treat the injured and provide immediate relief to the affected families,” he said. The disaster is a major challenge for Shah’s five-month-old government but officials said the country had systems and officials who have experience in handling such tragedies, including the 2015 earthquake that killed nearly 9,000 people. Additional input from AFP

Four-wicket Robinson stars as Pakistan collapse in second Test. Ollie Robinson took a sensational 4-11 in 13 overs as Pakistan collapsed to 110 all out in the second Test against England at Lord’s on Friday. But on a day when 13 wickets fell in total, England then slumped to 13-2 in their second innings on a pitch still offering significant seam movement. England, however, had recovered to 81-3 — an overall lead of 261 runs — when bad light forced an early close to the second day. The hosts are seeking an unassailable 2-0 lead in a three-match series. Robinson was well-supported by fast bowler Jofra Archer, who did the initial damage in a return of 3-26, and fellow paceman Josh Tongue, who finished with 2-27 after making a Test-best 30 not out at number 11 earlier on Friday. England’s Ollie Robinson (2L) celebrates with teammates after taking the wicket of Pakistan’s Khurram Shahzad on day two of the second Test match between England and Pakistan at Lord’s cricket ground in Leeds, London on August 28, 2026. Opener Azan Awais top-scored for the tourists with a determined 46, after he was dropped on eight in the slips by Harry Brook. Saud Shakeel’s 16 was the only other double-figure contribution by a Pakistan batsman. An innings lasting a mere 37.2 overs ended with Pakistan nine wickets down after opener Imam-ul-Haq was unable to bat following a calf injury suffered when fielding on Thursday. Gus Atkinson (45) and Tongue had earlier frustrated Pakistan with a tenth-wicket partnership of 47. Archer made the breakthrough when a flat-footed Shan Masood, opening in place of Imam, edged a 146 kilometre per hour full-length delivery to wicket-keeper Jamie Smith for one. Tongue then struck with what became the last ball before lunch when Abdullah Shafique was caught behind to leave Pakistan 16-2. Azam falls cheaply on return Pakistan captain Babar Azam got off the mark in style as he belted an 88 mph Tongue delivery through the covers for four before a flashing drive off Atkinson also sped to the boundary. That was as good as it got for Azam, who missed Pakistan’s crushing innings and 103-run defeat in the first Test at Headingley last week with a finger injury, before he nicked Tongue to a diving Jordan Cox at third slip. England’s Jordan Cox (2L) holds on to a catch to dismiss Pakistan’s Babar Azam on day two of the second Test match between England and Pakistan at Lord’s cricket ground in Leeds, London on August 28, 2026. — AFP Pakistan were 30-3, having been dismissed for 171 and 135 at Headingley. Both Shakeel and Mohammad Rizwan were lbw to Robinson before Ali Usman played on to Archer. Pakistan then lost a flurry of wickets, Archer ending the innings in emphatic fashion when he knocked over Mohammad Abbas’s off-stump. Khurram Shahzad gave Pakistan a glimmer of hope with 2-5 in two overs after Ben Duckett (one) mistimed a half-volley to mid-off before Cox (11) was lbw on review. England captain Joe Root, not for the first time in his long career, came in with his side in trouble, at 13-2. Together with Emilio Gay, he kept Pakistan at bay until, on 24, he was plumb lbw to a nip-back ball from Mohammad Ali — the ninth time in 12 Test innings the England great had been leg before wicket. Next ball Brook was also given out lbw to Ali, but the batsman’s review revealed a huge inside edge. England’s Gus Atkinson plays a shot to be caught out for 45 runs on day two of the second Test match between England and Pakistan at Lord’s cricket ground in Leeds, London on August 28, 2026. — AFP In the morning, England resumed on 248-9 after fifties from Smith and Cox helped them recover from a top-order collapse caused by veteran seamer Abbas’s superb burst of 3-4 in 16 balls after Pakistan won the toss. Atkinson was 34 not out and Tongue unbeaten on one. Tongue expertly glanced Ali for four and drilled Abbas through the covers for another boundary, with England’s last-wicket duo largely untroubled by a Pakistan seam attack lacking raw speed. Azam belatedly turned to left-arm spinner Ali Usman. Atkinson, who has a Test century at Lord’s to his credit, drove Usman’s third ball Friday for four but holed out off the next.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs342.02 per litre while HSD will cost Rs371.44 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to a Petroleum Division notification, the new prices will be applicable from Aug 29 to Aug 31. The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

'Profound consequences': Indus Water Treaty must not be weaponised, FM Dar warns India. WASHINGTON: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday warned that any attempt to deprive Pakistan of waters “rightfully allocated to it” under the Indus Waters Treaty would have “profound consequences for regional peace and security”. The IWT has come under strain since India announced in 2025 that it was placing its treaty obligations in abeyance. The announcement followed an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam that killed 26 tourists — an incident New Delhi blamed on Islamabad without evidence. For its part, Pakistan strongly denied the allegations and called for a neutral investigation. In his virtual address to a Washington seminar on “The Indus Waters Treaty: South Asian Security at the Crossroads”, he declared that Pakistan would strongly safeguard its “legitimate rights and interests” under the treaty and international law. FM Dar said the 1960 agreement remained “valid, binding and fully operative” despite India’s unilateral decision in April 2025 to place it “in abeyance”. “The treaty contains no provision permitting either party to unilaterally suspend or place it in abeyance,” he said, adding that neither country could, “through a unilateral political declaration, extinguish obligations solemnly undertaken under international law.” FM Dar said the issue went beyond the bilateral relationship, arguing that it concerned “the sanctity of treaties” and “confidence in international law”. “If solemn treaty obligations can simply be set aside whenever political relations deteriorate, the very purpose of concluding the treaties is undermined,” he said. He also stressed that geography made cooperation unavoidable, noting that “states cannot alter the direction in which rivers flow”. “That is precisely why rules matter,” FM Dar said, urging the international community to preserve treaty-based water governance in South Asia. The foreign minister further said the treaty had survived wars, military crises, diplomatic breakdowns and prolonged political tensions for more than six decades because both countries had understood that water on which “hundreds of millions of lives depend” was too fundamental to be subjected to fluctuations in political relations. “Today, however, that principle faces its gravest challenge,” he said. FM Dar said Pakistan’s position was clear and consistent and that treaty-based proceedings had continued despite India’s assertion of “abeyance”, reinforcing the principle that “unilateral action cannot displace an agreed legal framework”. Pakistan has pursued arbitration over disputes concerning Indian hydroelectric projects on the Western Rivers, particularly Kishenganga and Ratle. The Court of Arbitration at The Hague has continued proceedings, with earlier rulings addressing its jurisdiction and questions concerning the interpretation and application of the treaty. The treaty allocates the three eastern rivers to India and the three western rivers, including the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, primarily to Pakistan, subject to specified Indian uses. FM Dar said resorting to the Permanent Indus Commission, a neutral expert or a Court of Arbitration “is not an act of confrontation” but “the implementation of the very legal framework to which both countries agreed and are bound”. “Pakistan has consistently sought to resolve differences through dialogue, diplomacy and the mechanisms provided under the Treaty,” he said. He said the dispute was especially serious because Pakistan’s agriculture, food security, energy production, livelihoods and economic development depended heavily on the Indus River system. “The Indus Basin is the lifeline of more than 250 million Pakistanis,” Dar said. “Water security for Pakistan is therefore inseparable from economic security, food security and, ultimately, national security.” Against this backdrop, he warned that unilateral interference with the treaty could affect not only South Asian stability but also create “a dangerous precedent for treaty relations everywhere”. “International agreements derive their value from certainty and predictability,” FM Dar said. “If solemn treaty obligations can simply be set aside whenever political relations deteriorate, the very purpose of concluding the treaties is undermined.” He linked the dispute to climate change, saying Pakistan was already among the world’s most water-stressed countries and faced changing precipitation patterns, glacial retreat, floods, droughts and increasing hydrological variability. “These realities should compel greater and stronger cooperation,” he said, calling for improved data-sharing, sustained technical engagement and greater transparency. “But,” he added, “adaptation cannot mean abandonment of agreed legal rights and obligations”. Dar added that the treaty’s dispute-settlement architecture had been designed precisely to withstand disagreements between the two countries. “The answer to disagreement was therefore built into the Treaty itself: dialogue, technical engagement and lawful dispute resolution,” he said. The foreign minister also emphasised that treaty implementation “was never made contingent upon political convenience”. For Pakistan, he said, the preferred approach remained “law over unilateralism, dialogue over confrontation, and cooperation over coercion”. At the same time, Dar sought to make clear that Islamabad considered its water rights a matter of vital national importance. “Any attempt to deprive Pakistan of the waters rightfully allocated to it under the Indus Waters Treaty would have profound consequences for regional peace and security,” he said. “Pakistan will safeguard its legitimate rights and interests under the treaty and international law.” Dar further stated that the IWT had demonstrated for more than 65 years that Pakistan and India could insulate a vital shared resource from their wider political relationship. “That achievement should not be dismantled. It should be preserved,” he said. He proposed three principles for the way forward: that the treaty be “respected and implemented in letter and spirit”; that all questions, differences and disputes be addressed through its mechanisms; and that Pakistan and India restore and strengthen “technical engagement, transparency and data-sharing”. “These are not unreasonable demands,” Dar said. “They are the requirements of an agreement solemnly concluded by two sovereign states and sustained for more than six decades.” He also invoked Pakistan’s recent diplomatic role in facilitating dialogue during the US-Iran crisis, saying the effort reflected Islamabad’s belief that difficult disputes should ultimately be addressed through “engagement, diplomacy and peaceful settlement”. “Pakistan seeks to be a force for peace and stability, in South Asia and beyond,” he said. Dar concluded by urging that the Indus remains “a source of life, livelihood and civilisation, not a fault line for confrontation”. “Shared waters must never be weaponised,” he said. “They should remain a bridge between nations, governed by law, sustained through cooperation, and protected for generations to come.”

Govt seeks fresh financing plan for ML-1 section. ISLAMABAD: The proposed construction of the 460km Rohri-Multan section of the long-delayed Karachi-Peshawar Main Line-1 railway project, estimated to cost more than Rs450 billion, came under review on Friday as the government explored financing options other than the long-awaited Chinese funding. A high-level committee led by Planning and Development Minister Ahsan Iqbal did not clear the proposal prepared by the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) after noting that the cost of locomotives, coaches and their operation would be over and above the Rs450bn estimate for the railway section. The minister also ordered an independent third-party review of the cost estimates. “The meeting was also briefed on the proposal of the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) to develop the Rohri-Multan section of ML-1 through private investment. The meeting was informed that the estimated cost of the Rohri-Multan section is over Rs450 billion,” an official statement said. “The meeting reviewed various financing options for the completion of the ML-1 project, including the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP), foreign financing, public-private partnership (PPP), financing through local commercial banks and the domestic capital markets,” it added. The committee also deliberated on the formulation of a comprehensive financing plan for the project. The meeting was held by a committee constituted on the prime minister’s directions to explore financing options for the Rohri-Multan section. Mr Iqbal said the upgradation and modernisation of ML-1 remained a key government priority and called for a viable financing strategy. Sources said the minister expressed displeasure over participation by some ministries at the additional secretary level and directed that federal secretaries attend the committee’s next meeting. The railways secretary was asked to come up with a proper estimate for locomotives, coaches and other rolling stock, along with financing options and an assessment of how much funding Pakistan Railways could generate through its own marketing plan. Mr Iqbal also directed that a comprehensive feasibility study be conducted by a credible independent third party to assess the project’s technical, financial and economic viability and help develop a sustainable financing model. According to the statement, the Ministry of Railways was also asked to assess future requirements for locomotives, freight rolling stock and passenger coaches, including the financing required, and incorporate them into an integrated plan. The minister observed that continued reductions in the development budget were affecting projects of national importance, underscoring the need to make better use of available resources and explore alternative financing mechanisms. The meeting was also briefed on the condition of the railway track and accidents attributed to deteriorating infrastructure. Published in Dawn, August 29th, 2026

Owners to be liable if terrorists use their land: Bugti. QUETTA: Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarf­raz Bugti has warned owners of vineyards and other private properties in Mas­t­ung that they will be treated as facilitators if their land is used to launch attacks on security forces or provincial ministers. Speaking to the media after inaugurating digital initiatives at the Central Police Office on Friday, CM Bugti said the government did not want to take action that could harm ordinary citizens, as terrorists often used civilians as human shields. How­ever, he said property owners could not claim ignorance if attacks were launched from their land. “If a security forces’ convoy or the home minister is attacked from a vineyard, the owners cannot say they did not know terrorists were present on their land,” he said. He said vineyard owners had repeatedly been warned and, if private properties continued to be used for terrorism, the government would have to consider relocating people on a large scale or eliminating vineyards being used for terrorist activities. “The blood of Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and police personnel is extremely sacred,” CM Bugti said, adding that the government would not tolerate security personnel being martyred while private properties were used for terrorism. Meanwhile, the chief minister said Balochistan was moving towards maximum digitalisation of governance to improve transparency and public services. Eight existing Balochistan Police apps had been upgraded and eight new ones introduced to facilitate access to the criminal justice system and enable citizens to lodge complaints. A women’s safety application allows users to trigger an emergency alert with a single click, notifying their families and police. Mr Bugti announced an awareness campaign targeting female students, working women and travellers. Digital facilities for families of police martyrs would also provide direct contact with them and help identify their welfare needs. Other services include Khidmat Markaz, hotel and travel facilities, and the IGP Police Complaint Cell. Mr Bugti announced Rs5 million in cash rew­ards for officers and personnel involved in the digitalisation drive and allocated Rs50m for further digitalisation of Balo­­chistan Police. He said CCTV and Safe City cameras had helped trace suspects in murder cases and contributed to arrests following major terrorist attacks. A Safe City Authority had been established under the relevant legislation and integrated with law-enforcement agencies. Regarding the tehsildar recruitment process, Mr Bugti said an internal error had been detected and a committee formed in coordination with the Public Service Com­mission would submit its report within seven to 10 days. He reiterated that the government would not compromise on merit, even at the cost of political losses. Citing recent Balochistan Rev­enue Authority recruitment, he said 20 to 25 people from his constituency had applied, but none of them was selected, demonstrating that the process was merit-based. Published in Dawn, August 29th, 2026

PCB complains after interview with Imran’s sons telecast during Test. KARACHI: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has lodged a formal complaint with the broadcaster after an interview with former prime minister and cricketer Imran Khan’s sons was telecast during the first day of the second Test against England at Lord’s. According to reports in ESPN Cricinfo , The Guardian and other UK-based publications, the board had complained to Sky Sports and considered instructing the Pakistan team not to take the field after lunch in protest. The interview, recorded at Lord’s on the eve of the Test and broadcast during a rain-delayed lunch interval on Thursday, focused on concerns over Imran’s health after nearly three years in custody. The brothers spoke of significant deterioration in their father’s eyesight and said they feared for his life. According to UK media reports, Pakistan weighed not taking the field after lunch on day one in protest However, the PCB maintained silence over the move, and did not respond to multiple requests for comment. According to the ESPN Cricinfo report, the PCB contacted Sky Sports before the lunch interval to object to the planned broadcast and warned that Pakistan’s players might refuse to return for the afternoon session. Sky Sports initially delayed the broadcast while discussions took place but eventually aired the interview in full. By the time it ended, Pakistan’s players were preparing to resume play at 2:40pm local time and returned to the field as scheduled. The England and Wales Cricket Board was made aware of the complaint and helped ensure that the match continued without disruption, the report said. Pakistan’s state broadcaster, PTV , which holds the domestic broadcasting rights, did not air the interview. ESPN Cricinfo also reported that the PCB considered raising the matter with the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. Meanwhile, Australian captain Pat Cummins became the latest prominent cricketer to publicly support calls for Imran Khan to receive proper medical care. In a post on X on Friday, quoting former Australian captain Greg Chappell, Cummins wrote: “Adding my support here to GC and the other former international captains. I hope the court ordered medical assessment be allowed to run its course, and that family visits continue. I hope Imran Khan is treated with the dignity anyone deserves.” Cummins is the first active international captain to publicly back the campaign. His comments came days after a letter signed by around 21 former international captains, including Atherton, Greg and Ian Chappell, Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev, Allan Border, Clive Lloyd and Alastair Cook, was sent to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The former captains, representing India, Australia, England, the West Indies and New Zealand, called for the completion of an independent medical assessment ordered by the Supreme Court, including examination by Imran’s personal doctors.
