Sabalenka shrugs off struggles, eyes historic third straight US Open crown. NEW YORK (AP) — Aryna Sabalenka has appeared to be having fun everywhere but the tennis court lately. Her Instagram account is filled with photos where she is fashionably dressed in beautiful settings, or lounging in a bikini in relaxing ones. Life looks great. On the court, it's as bad as it's been in a while. The top-ranked women's player hasn't even gotten past the fourth round of her last few tournaments, and she hardly looks ready to become the first player to win three straight U.S. Open titles since Serena Williams from 2012-14. Sabalenka doesn't sound concerned. She sounds defiant. Her response to those wondering what's wrong with her game: “Maybe there’s something wrong with people,” she said. To those who don't like the black mesh-covered outfit she's wearing on the court in New York: “Who cares about people, right? All matters for me is that I love it,” Sabalenka responded. Sabalenka looked headed for a superb season at the start of the year. She lost in the Australian Open final to Elena Rybakina, but then won back-to-back hard-court titles at Indian Wells and Miami. Even after she was knocked out by Naomi Osaka in the fourth round at Wimbledon, it was assumed Sabalenka would quickly return to form when she came back to North America and the hard courts where her power is so tough to handle. Then she was upset by Ekaterina Alexandrova in the fourth round in Toronto and blew leads in both sets and was ousted by Sara Bejlek in Cincinnati, appearing frustrated at times with her game the way she used to earlier in her career. She won't specify what was wrong, but hinted that everything wasn't right. “It wasn’t the best period. I don’t want to defend myself, but obviously I just don’t want to talk about that period. I’ve been dealing with several things,” Sabalenka said. “But who cares, right? Yeah, I didn’t perform my best. These tough lessons are definitely going to make me way, way stronger and working even harder. I work on my mental side of the game. I was trying to reset my mind and to come back stronger, so it’s only going to make me stronger. It’s only a matter of time for me to come back.” It wouldn't be a surprise if it was in New York, where she won the title for the first time in 2024 by beating Jessica Pegula in the final. She defended it last year by topping Amanda Anisimova. Reaching the top has given the 28-year-old from Belarus plenty of benefits off the court. Endorsement deals and photo shoots. Vacations during the season to Greece with her fiance. It gives critics who see Sabalenka detail all of that on social media the opportunity to question whether it's too much fun and not enough work. “She’s still No. 1 in the world. So I think the results are there,” said Paula Badosa, Sabalenka's friend on tour who has been pictured in some of those photos with her. “Of course, everyone is going to expect for her to win every tournament. That’s very, very difficult. And at the moment, that one player is not winning what they expected. Of course, they’re saying that it’s because of the photo shoots or the TikToks and all this stuff, and I’m not going to lie, she’s been doing that since she was maybe out of the top 100. And when she was winning, nobody says anything, you know? And when she loses a couple of matches, it’s because of that. I think it’s none of it.” The No. 1 ranking is in jeopardy after Sabalenka's summer swoon. She may need to make a deep run in New York with the likes of Rybakina and Pegula gaining on her. Sabalenka has done it before. She may be down now but doesn't sound like she plans to stay there. “Well, that’s the beauty of the sport,” she said. “Throw tough challenges at me, I will come back only stronger.”

What to know about the backlash against Infantino. MONACO (AP) — Gianni Infantino, the increasingly embattled FIFA president, was everywhere in the conversations as European soccer leaders gathered this week in Monaco for the Champions League draw. UEFA, the European soccer confederation, is spearheading the backlash against Infantino over his failed World Cup sell-off plan that created a deep rift in the sport one month ago. Many of its member federations have withdrawn their support for the FIFA leader, who is up for re-election in March 2027, and some have called for his resignation. Infantino has not given any indication he plans to step down. Here’s what to know about the growing pushback against the FIFA president. UEFA ramps up the pressure with legal action On Thursday, UEFA escalated the situation by revealing that it is preparing a possible criminal complaint against the FIFA president in Switzerland – where the organization is based – for alleged mismanagement. The European soccer confederation filed requests in U.S. courts seeking evidence about Infantino’s secretive plan to give private investors led by Joshua Kushner a stake in the profits of future World Cups and other FIFA tournaments for $4.2 billion. FIFA withdrew the proposal on Aug. 1, just days after it was made public, after intense pushback. UEFA’s lawyers called the plan “a vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA’s most valuable assets to the detriment of FIFA, its members, and other parties within the football family.” FIFA did not comment on UEFA’s move, which increases pressure on Infantino and puts other FIFA staffers at risk of legal exposure relating to a project that its now-fired chief operating officer said was Infantino’s idea. It also means Kushner, the younger brother of U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, faces increased scrutiny at a time when he is involved in a $12 billion takeover deal for the Los Angeles Lakers. Some of Infantino’s critics want him to step down before the vote. “Infantino is polarizing the world in a way we haven’t seen in history,” Norwegian soccer federation president Lise Klaveness said in Monaco. Norway was the first FIFA member federation explicitly asking Infantino to resign in the wake of the World Cup investment plan. Infantino’s re-election no longer a foregone conclusion Just months ago, ahead of the World Cup in the U.S., Canada and Mexico, Infantino was cruising toward an uncontested election win next March, with a clear majority of FIFA members backing him. Things look less certain now, with UEFA, Asian confederation AFC and CONCACAF, the governing body for soccer North and Central America and the Caribbean, accusing the FIFA president of “ deception.” Together those groups represent a majority of FIFA member federations. However, several AFC and CONCACAF members have declared continued support for Infantino as have a series of soccer federations in Africa and South America, many of which depend on FIFA funding. He needs just over half of FIFA’s 211 member federations to vote for him to be re-elected. Infantino spent last weekend in the Dominican Republic meeting FIFA members from the Caribbean, despite a request by FIFA’s Canadian vice president and CONCACAF leader Victor Montagliani not to visit. The Kushner-backed $4.2 billion investment would have funded $20 million offers to each of FIFA’s 211 member federations. That would be game-changing money for the 25 members in the Caribbean. On Wednesday, Infantino’s Instagram account showed he was in Vietnam. So far, no challenger has emerged to run against Infantino. The candidate deadline is Nov. 18, four months before election day in Rabat, Morocco, which is a FIFA stronghold. Key dates on the soccer calendar Infantino would be expected in Poland soon for the FIFA-organized Under-20 Women’s World Cup played from Sept. 5-27. But one Polish soccer official in Monaco said they had no idea of Infantino’s plans to be in the country. It is a long-standing quip that FIFA staff read Instagram to learn where he is. UEFA has an executive committee meeting Sept. 15 in Thessaloniki, Greece. The influential European Football Clubs group meets Sept. 29 in Copenhagen. It is close to sealing a joint venture deal with FIFA overseeing the 2029 Club World Cup that Infantino wants to be worth $2 billion. The clubs’ leader Nasser al-Khelaifi, from Paris Saint-Germain, is a key ally of UEFA and also a member of the government of Qatar which has backed Infantino in this crisis.

Not your usual cup of matcha. Matcha is usually associated with lattes, desserts, and the popular familiar green-hued treats that have become fixtures on menus. Ebi10 and The Matcha Tokyo Philippines, however, are taking the Japanese ingredient in a different direction — bringing it into savory territory. Until Sept. 23, the two brands are joining forces for a limited-time menu that pairs Ebi10’s Japanese comfort food with The Matcha Tokyo’s premium, 100 percent organic matcha. Created with Chef Mikko Reyes of Ebi10, the collaboration explores matcha’s earthy flavor and gentle bitterness alongside seafood, tempura, and other familiar Japanese ingredients. The result is a menu that treats matcha as more than a beverage or dessert ingredient. At the center of the collaboration is the Mentai Matcha Jumbo Tempura, featuring two jumbo white shrimps coated in matcha tempura batter, filled with mentaiko and served with organic matcha salt. The dish brings together the briny richness of mentaiko, the sweetness of shrimp and the subtle bitterness of matcha in a crisp bite. The Matcha Scallop Popcorn takes the same approach with local scallops. The seafood is coated in matcha tempura batter and served with organic matcha salt, fried nori, and sesame yuzu aioli. The citrus and creamy sesame notes provide balance to the earthiness of the matcha while allowing the natural sweetness of the scallops to come through. Matcha also makes its way into dessert. The Banana Tempura with Matcha Custard Cream pairs Ebi10’s warm, crisp banana tempura with silky matcha custard cream and organic matcha sugar, keeping the green tea flavor at the center of the dish. “Matcha is something people usually associate with drinks and desserts, so we wanted to have fun with the idea and show how well it can work with savory food too,” said Mica Viray-Aguila, managing partner of Ebi10 during the press preview last Aug. 25. “Working with The Matcha Tokyo gave us the chance to bring together what both brands do best and create something familiar, but with a completely new flavor.” For The Matcha Tokyo Philippines CEO Charles Paw, the collaboration is also about finding new ways for people to experience matcha. “I’m a firm believer of the quote from James Beard that says, ‘Food is our common ground, a universal experience,’” Paw said. “That’s why we’re always excited to find new ways for people to experience matcha, especially through collaborations like this one with Ebi10 that bring different ideas together.” The Matcha Tokyo, established in 2018, brings premium organic matcha into modern everyday life. Rooted in Japanese matcha culture, the brand describes its approach as a contemporary take on how matcha is enjoyed, with its philosophy centered on “Matcha for a healthy and beautiful life.” Ebi10, meanwhile, is a Japanese comfort food restaurant inspired by a family trip to Osaka and a love for freshly made tempura. Since opening its first location in Poblacion, Makati, the restaurant has expanded across Metro Manila and beyond, offering approachable Japanese dishes made with the Filipino palate in mind. The Ebi10 x The Matcha Tokyo Philippines menu will be available at all Ebi10 branches from Aug. 27 to Sept. 23.

LPA may enter PAR this weekend, develop into tropical cyclone—PAGASA. A low-pressure area (LPA), which has a moderate chance of developing into a tropical cyclone, may enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) this weekend, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Saturday, Aug. 29. According to PAGASA weather specialist Veronica Torres, the LPA outside PAR was last spotted at 3 a.m. about 1,080 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon. “Ito ngang low-pressure area na ito ay katamtaman ‘yung tiyansa na maging isang ganap na bagyo. And then, possible din na pumasok ito ng ating area of responsibility this weekend (This low-pressure area has a moderate chance of developing into a tropical cyclone. It may also enter our area of responsibility this weekend),” she said. “Kaya patuloy pa rin tayong mag-antabay sa mga update ng PAGASA (That is why we should continue monitoring updates from PAGASA),” she added. PAGASA, meanwhile, is also monitoring another LPA inside PAR, which was last located about 520 kilometers north-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, as of 3 a.m. Torres noted that the LPA was already near the PAR boundary and could leave the country’s monitoring area within the next few hours or days. “Nakikita nga natin na napakalapit na nga nitong low-pressure area na ito sa boundary ng ating PAR line at posibleng lumabas na ng ating Philippine Area of Responsibility sa mga susunod na sandali o mga susunod na araw (We can see that this low-pressure area is already very close to the PAR boundary and may leave the Philippine Area of Responsibility within the next few hours or days),” she said. The weather specialist said the LPA has a low chance of developing into a tropical cyclone within the next 24 hours. “At if ever man maging bagyo ito, ito na ay nasa labas ng ating area of responsibility (If it develops into a tropical cyclone, it will already be outside our area of responsibility),” said Torres. The state weather bureau said the southwest monsoon, locally called “habagat,” continues to affect Luzon and the Visayas. “Samantala, ‘yung southwest monsoon o habagat ay patuloy pa rin ang epekto sa Luzon pati na rin sa Visayas, kaya asahan nga natin ‘yung mga malalakas na pag-ulan dala pa rin ng southwest monsoon, mostly sa western sections ng Luzon (Meanwhile, the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to affect Luzon and the Visayas, so we can expect heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon, mostly over the western sections of Luzon),” she said. In Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 13 issued at 5 a.m. on Saturday, PAGASA placed Bataan, Zambales, Pampanga, and a portion of Bulacan under a red rainfall warning due to rains brought by the southwest monsoon. Metro Manila, Rizal, Cavite, and portions of Tarlac, Bulacan, Batangas, and Laguna were under an orange warning, while portions of Tarlac, Laguna, and Batangas were placed under a yellow warning. Per PAGASA, a red warning means serious flooding is expected in flood-prone areas, while an orange warning indicates that flooding is threatening and a yellow warning means flooding is possible.

Eight PH films shortlisted for Oscars 2027 consideration. The Film Academy of the Philippines (FDCP) has narrowed down submissions for consideration to the 99th Academy Award's Best International Feature Film category, Eight films have been named with the country’s official entry set to be announced on Sept. 4. The contenders include films tackling Philippine history, identity, relationships, social issues, and contemporary life. Among them is “58th,” Carl Joseph Papa’s animated docu-drama centered on the 2009 Maguindanao Massacre, told through the perspective of one of the missing victim's daughter. “58th” has screened at several international festivals including Rotterdam and Annecy, as well as the Oscar-qualifying Doc Edge. Jade Castro’s “All the Things I Leave You (Patawid),” an Ilocano-language BL film, is also in contention. “Filipiñana,” directed by Rafael Manuel, recently opened in Philippine cinemas after making its way through the international festival circuit. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Dramatic Special Jury Award for Creative Vision. It follows a young woman working at a posh golf course. “I’mPerfect,” directed by Sigrid Andrea Bernardo, is another contender. The film was a Metro Manila Film Festival winner. It centers on a couple with Down syndrome. “Manila’s Finest,” directed by Raymond Red, is also on the shortlist. The film is set shortly before the First Quarter Storm. Jerrold Tarog’s “Quezon,” meanwhile, is the third installment in the director's so-called “Bayaniverse” franchise and stars Jericho Rosales as Manuel L. Quezon, the Philippines’ second president. Hilda Koronel marks her return to film with “Sisa,” directed by Jun Robles Lana. The veteran actress plays a woman believed to be mentally unstable who secretly works as a spy for Filipino revolutionaries during the Philippine-American War. Rounding out the contenders is Lawrence Fajardo’s “Silenced Nights,” inspired by the 2017 killing of Kian delos Santos during the Duterte government’s war on drugs. Film Academy Director-General Paolo Villaluna said the eight films present different perspectives on the Filipino experience. “They look at our history, the issues we continue to face and the ways Filipinos deal with questions of power, identity, love, freedom and survival,” Villaluna said. He added that each film has “its own voice and approach,” with the potential to connect with audiences outside the Philippines. The eight films will undergo evaluation by a selection committee organized by the Film Academy and composed of local film industry experts as approved by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. The committee will consider each submission based on artistic merit, cultural relevance and its potential for an international campaign. Despite decades of submissions, no Philippine film has been nominated for or made the shortlist for the Academy Awards’ International Feature Film category. Past Philippine entries include “Dekada ’70,” “Heneral Luna,” “Ang Babae sa Septic Tank,” and “Magellan,” which was considered one of the country’s strongest chances of making the first cut. Shortlist for the Philippines’ Oscars 2027 entry: “58th” — directed by Carl Joseph Papa “All the Things I Leave You (Patawid)” — directed by Jade Castro “Filipiñana” — directed by Rafael Manuel “I’mPerfect” — directed by Sigrid Andrea Bernardo “Manila’s Finest” — directed by Raymond Red “Quezon” — directed by Jerrold Tarog “Silenced Nights” — directed by Lawrence Fajardo “Sisa” — directed by Jun Robles Lana

New QCPD chief assumes command. Police Brig. Gen. Christopher F. Olazo assumed his post as Quezon City Police District (QCPD) director on Friday, Aug. 28, succeeding Police Brig. Gen. Randy Glenn Silvio. A Philippine National Police Academy (PNPA) Kabalikat Class of 1998 alumnus, Olazo formally took over the district during a turnover ceremony at the QCPD Hinirang Social Hall in Camp Karingal, Quezon City. The event was attended by Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte and presided over by National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) officer-in-charge Police Brig. Gen. Christopher N. Abrahano. Also present were National Police Commission (NAPOLCOM) Vice Chairperson and Executive Officer Rafael Calinisan, Congressman Ralph “Raffy” Tulfo, and other officials and guests. In his inaugural message, Olazo vowed to lead by example, uphold accountability, and maintain professionalism in keeping Quezon City safe. “I understand the demands of this District and the importance of maintaining the standards that the QCPD has established through the years. To the QCitizen, I assure you that the QCPD will remain committed to maintaining peace and order, preventing and responding to crime, protecting our communities, and providing professional and accessible police service,” Olazo said. Before assuming the QCPD directorship, Olazo held various key positions in the Philippine National Police (PNP), including chief of police of Bacoor City and Taguig City, QCPD battalion commander, provincial director of the Cavite Police Provincial Office, and senior police assistant to the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) secretary. Belmonte welcomed Olazo to his new post and assured him of the continued support of the Quezon City government as he leads the district in upholding the city’s standards of public safety and public service. Silvio, in his final message as QCPD director, expressed pride in what he and his personnel accomplished during his tenure and thanked them for their trust, support, and commitment. Abrahano also directed the regionwide adoption of the Investigation Solution Automatic Verification (ISAV), an initiative implemented under Silvio’s leadership, to further strengthen police operations. He said the directive supports the initiatives of PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. aimed at achieving three key outcomes: less crime, faster response, and better-behaved policemen. Under Olazo’s leadership, the QCPD is expected to build on its gains, pursue innovations, and further strengthen its delivery of responsive police services to QCitizens.

Former Ecuadorian President Lenín Moreno sentenced to 5 years for corruption. QUITO, Ecuador (AP) — Former Ecuadorian President Lenín Moreno was sentenced Friday to 5 years in prison after a court found him guilty of accepting bribes from a Chinese company in exchange for helping it secure a contract to build a hydroelectric plant. Moreno, who was present for the reading of the verdict, is 73 years old and has a physical disability that prevents him from walking. He will serve the sentence under house arrest. Moreno was convicted as a direct participant in the bribery scheme during his tenure as vice president under Rafael Correa. His wife and daughter, two brothers and a brother-in-law were convicted as accomplices. The wife and daughter each received 30-month sentences. All were ordered to repay triple what they received illicitly within a period of 90 days. Moreno is the third former Ecuadorian president to be sentenced for corruption, though he was tried for crimes before reaching the presidency. Correa was sentenced in 2020 to eight years in prison in a bribery case involving Brazilian construction giant Odebrecht but remains in Belgium, where he has lived for years. Former President Jamil Mahuad was also sentenced in 2014 to eight years for misuse of public funds. Another former president, Abdalá Bucaram, is awaiting sentencing after being convicted of organized crime. Prosecutors said a corruption network operated from 2008 to 2018, collecting bribes equal to 4% of the value of the project carried out by Sinohydro. They said the money was distributed through domestic and international transactions to public officials and other beneficiaries, including Moreno. Sinohydro began building the roughly $2 billion Coca Codo Sinclair hydroelectric plant in 2010 and handed it over to Ecuador in 2016. The project has since faced criticism over structural defects. Moreno, a tourism entrepreneur, rose to national prominence in 2007 when he became vice president under Correa, who governed Ecuador for a decade. Moreno served until 2013, when Jorge Glas succeeded him. In 2017, Moreno won the presidency as a candidate of the Correísta movement founded around Correa, with Glas as his running mate. Glas later left office and is now serving a prison sentence for corruption.

1st-Half Births in Japan Rise for 1st Time in 11 Years. Tokyo, Aug. 28 (Jiji Press)--The number of births in Japan rose in the first half of the year for the first time in 11 years, health ministry data showed Friday in a sign that the figure’s rapid decline is ending. The preliminary data showed that the number of births in the January-June period edged up by 2,788, or 0.8 pct, from a year before to 342,068, still below 400,000 for the fifth consecutive year. The rise may have reflected increases in marriages in 2024-2025. The number of births by Japanese nationals in Japan stood at 671,236 in 2025, marking a record low for the 10th straight year, according to data released in June. The size of decrease shrank to 2.2 pct from around 5 pct since 2022, however. The number of marriages grew by 418 to 238,979 in the first six months of the year, while that of divorces fell by 3,578 to 90,177. Deaths totaled 778,982. The natural decrease in the population, or the number of deaths minus that of births, was 436,914. The preliminary data includes births by foreigners in Japan and those by Japanese nationals who live overseas. Revised data, which will be disclosed later, only counts births by Japanese nationals who live in the country. The annual number of births in Japan has been on a declining trend since 1975. It went below one million in 2016 and fell below 700,000 in 2024.

Japan to Set Up Multifunctional Defense Hub in Hiroshima. Tokyo, Aug. 28 (Jiji Press)--Japan’s Defense Ministry on Friday concluded a contract with Nippon Steel Corp. to acquire a former plant site in Kure in Hiroshima Prefecture, western Japan, to develop a multifunctional defense complex there. The approximately 140-hectare land plot, Nippon Steel's former Setouchi Works Kure Area site, is expected to host Self-Defense Forces buildings, barracks, a defense equipment manufacturing facility, a supply depot and a heliport. The ministry will soon start accepting bids from companies for contracts to manufacture, maintain and repair defense equipment at the planned complex and engage in research and development there. The Kure area is an extremely important region for national security as it is home to major Maritime SDF facilities, Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said at a press conference. We aim to use (the planned complex) to fundamentally strengthen the country’s defense,” he added.

Monica Lorenzo builds for lasting value, with sustainability at the foundation. In real estate, what lasts isn’t just concrete and steel. For Monica Lorenzo, director for leisure and business development at Torre Lorenzo Development Corporation (TLDC), lasting value looks like something else entirely. It means developments that strengthen the communities around them, treat the environment as a partner rather than an obstacle, and still make sense to the people living there decades from now. It’s a simple enough principle on paper. Developments shouldn’t come at the expense of the people and places it’s supposed to serve. Living up to it is the harder part. A house built on lies falls with the first storm. The simple, almost proverbial line reflects a philosophy that would be profound in an industry where foundations, structures and promises carry heavy weight. Honesty, then, becomes both a simple and complicated word. And it is the exact word Monica Lorenzo, this year’s PropertyGuru Rising Star Awardee, gave when asked to describe the work virtue she lives by. “It is my personality. It is who I am,” she said. Monica works and lives by that same virtue. For her, success is not measured only by what is built. It is gauged by what endures; what continues to inspire, uplift and strengthen communities while caring for the planet. TLDC is the pioneer builder of premium university residences in the Philippines. What began as a desire to improve the cramped, unconducive living conditions of students in Metro Manila has grown into a full-scale residential and hospitality developer with projects across Manila, Lipa and Davao, partnering with Dusit International and The Ascott Limited of Singapore on its hospitality developments. For Monica, part of the appeal of real estate and hospitality has always been how tangible it is. “You really see what you created and what you’ve worked on. You see how your ideas are coming to reality.” But admittedly, that tangibility comes with a constant stream of challenges. Monica describes the company’s position as often introducing concepts to the Philippines that already existed elsewhere but had never quite landed here. Demanding discipline as much as ambition, the company is selective about where it puts its resources. “We are very choosy and picky as to where we decide to put our resources, investment and energy,” she said. “We operate on the fact that each building is a better version of the last.” She sees the Philippines’ young, increasingly upward mobile population as an opportunity to build things people never thought possible for themselves. It is a philosophy she traces directly back to her father, who once told her: “You have to show them it can get better. This is what we can give you.” When asked what motivates her, she said, “It is the sense of responsibility to help the company be the best it can be. I am not just an employee, and ties run deeper. This is something that my father built for the next generation, and I want to do the same. To pass it on and get it through to the next generation.” Being named PropertyGuru’s Rising Star, she says, is a welcome vote of confidence to that mission. “It helps build confidence that we are pulling things in the right direction. We are always evolving and changing and we’re not slowing down. There is so much we can do.” Learnings from the shoreline Monica’s understanding of environmental stewardship did not come from a classroom. It came from watching a place she loved slowly change. Her family’s island resort, now known as Dusit Thani Lubi Plantation, was somewhere she visited throughout her childhood. She vividly remembers the lush greenery and the vast shoreline. Over the years, she watched as the shoreline visibly retreated. She remembers how different the environment on that island was 20 years ago. Watching the changes firsthand raised an unavoidable question: What can be done to prevent further damage, so that the next generation can enjoy these same places? For her family, the answer was to act. The waters surrounding the island were designated a protected coral sanctuary, with strict bans on fishing and coral harvesting. Roughly 15 years later, the results speak for themselves. Fish populations have returned and the reefs that were once damaged by overfishing and bleaching are healthy again. That same resort now runs on the kind of sustainability infrastructure that sounded aspirational. On the island is a solar farm of 1,836 panels that supplies up to sixty percent of the resort’s energy needs.. This cuts roughly 985 metric tons of CO2 emissions a year. Heat recovery systems repurpose warmth from air-conditioning units to heat water for every room and villa. Through reverse osmosis and desalination systems, seawater is turned into the island’s drinking supply. Pools, pathways and roads are designed with sustainability in mind. This is the balance Monica tries to strike across every project: comfort and luxury that does not come at the planet’s expense. Listening before building Ask Monica what role culture and local context play in her projects, and she describes a process that starts long before the ground is broken. By talking to the people who already bought from them and to residents living in their buildings, and by asking what is working and what is not, the company stays in tune with where they are at. With that, they are able to adapt their plans and designs. “Flexibility matters,” she says, considering that a single building can take five or six years to complete. That same philosophy shapes how she thinks about the difference between a development and a destination. For Monica, real estate was never meant to be one-and-done. “It’s really a whole community; a whole masterplanned development,” she says, “because that is how you’re actually able to build a community.” In hospitality terms, she frames the challenge simply: getting someone to book that first stay. “We know, and we are confident enough in our brand, with our developments, and with our projects. Once they stay, they will want to come back.” Growth and environmental responsibility, in her view, were never meant to be separated. “It has to go hand in hand,” she says. She acknowledges that they play a direct role in the community and that it is their responsibility to take care of it. Every project, she says, comes with the same underlying question: How do we integrate ourselves and work together with the people already there to genuinely uplift the towns and barangays we invest in? Bridging old habits and new standards Real estate, by nature, is a slow-moving, brick-and-mortar industry, and Monica is candid about the limits that come with that. Sustainability, she points out, doesn’t only live in construction; it also lives in operations, planning and design. “Technology hasn’t caught up, “ she admits. “We can’t do things a hundred percent greener and sustainable given there are certain regulations that need to be met, and the environment we are constructing in, the weather, and all other factors.” Where the technology and the regulatory room exist, though, her team integrates it, steadily pushing each new building to be greener than the one before it. Building for the generations to come When Monica talks about legacy, she thinks of generations instead of years as the timeline. “We at TLDC are building things to last. We are building for the next generation,“ she says. The goal, as she puts it, is making sure a building still stands for the grandchildren of the people who first bought it. “If we build, we better do it right. It is a matter of being flexible and open to changes, so that whatever headwinds come, we will be able to adapt.” Her hope and optimism carry into how she talks about the future, for what these projects leave behind extends beyond the buildings themselves and to the land they are built on. “There is so much that can be done for the planet,” she says. “It is leaving the planet the same shape and condition it was given to us. We regenerate or replenish what is taken. It should not be a leaky bucket.” In the end, Monica’s one-word answer, honesty, brings the story back to its foundation. Honest about what a building can deliver. Honest about what a piece of land can and can’t withstand. And honest about what developers leave behind long after the ribbon has been cut. Because for Monica, building for the future is not only about making something that lasts. It is about making sure that what lasts is worth keeping. That means communities that are stronger, environments that are cared for, and places that future generations can still enjoy. That, perhaps, is the real foundation of lasting value.

Cone glad to be finally on the winning side of another cardiac finish. Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone heaved a sigh of relief as the Nationals avoided suffering the same heartbreak it had in the previous window. The Nationals had to go through a wringer to pull off a nerve-wracking 82-81 victory over Jordan and, more importantly, give its World Cup hopes a huge shot in the arm in the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian qualifiers. Gilas improved to 3-4, keeping their Top 3 hopes alive in Group E after surviving the Falcons in a game that had Cone recalling the pain of the Nationals’ 102-106 double-overtime loss to New Zealand in the last window. “It was fantastic. It was fun to be a part of. It was fun to be on this side of it, winning,” said Cone. “I know how tough it is against New Zealand. We were on the other side of it in the overtime game and losing this really, really, important qualifier so it’s good to be on this side of it,” he added. Gilas lost to the Tall Blacks on the road in the July window with Juan Gomez de Liaño delivering the big hits down the stretch. The Nationals were even one stop away from pulling off the upset but just couldn’t get the defensive break against the Kiwis in that game. That was also looking to be the case in the game against Jordan when Kevin Quiambao put Gilas up with a big triple down the stretch but the Falcons forced the Nationals to crucial turnovers in the waning seconds. The difference, however, this time was Gilas had its towering center Kai Sotto to anchor the defensive stand. Sotto rejected what could have been a go-ahead layup for Jordan’s Abdullah Olajuwon as the game clock expired. “I felt we had them on the ropes a few times. I feel we were ready to zoom off but turnover here and there kept them in the game and then we had to go down the stretch and come down to defense,” said Cone. “Kai came out and made the huge block in the end to win it for us.”

In Quake-Hit Kumamoto, Kids Back to School after Summer Break. Yatsushiro, Kumamoto Pref., Aug. 28 (Jiji Press)--Children returned to school after the summer break in Yatsushiro, Kumamoto Prefecture on Friday, a month after a major earthquake struck the southwestern Japan prefecture. The second term started at 40 elementary, junior high schools and special- needs schools in the city. Following the July 28 quake, which measured up to 7, the highest level on the Japanese seismic intensity scale, shelters were set up for evacuees at almost all of the schools. Shelters have been consolidated to make space for students to study aheadof the second term, according to the city’s education board. Currently, 16 schools in severely affected areas are hosting shelters. At Otago Elementary School, children arrived with smiles, rejoicing at reunion with friends. Shortly after 7 a.m., a girl was seen playing on an exercise bar in the schoolyard. Schoolchildren came down to the playground one after another, and some played soccer before school started. “I couldn’t play with friends because of the clearing work after the quake,” an 11-year-old girl in sixth grade said. “I’m happy that I can come to school.” In Yatsushiro, all six school lunch centers were damaged by the quake, and the kitchens in most schools are not usable. Until the lunch centers become operational, schools will serve vacuum-packed food for lunch, except for those with functioning kitchens. Students need to bring empty lunch boxes and chopsticks from home to use when they eat school lunch, because used dishes cannot be washed. In Kumamoto, 359 schools sustained damage from the quake, such as broken windows and cracks on buildings, the prefectural education board said. The second term will start on Tuesday at five elementary and junior high schools in the town of Hikawa.

La Mesa Dam nears overflow level amid heavy rains—PAGASA. The water level of La Mesa Dam in Quezon City rose to 79.81 meters on Saturday morning, Aug. 29, just 0.34 meters below its overflow elevation of 80.15 meters, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said. In its hydrological dam situationer issued at 10 a.m., PAGASA said a further increase in the dam’s water level was expected due to continued rainfall. “The water level of La Mesa Dam as of 10:00 AM is 79.81 m, which is still below its overflow elevation of 80.15 m,” PAGASA said. “However, due to the observed 24-hour rainfall of 137.5 mm and a forecast 24-hour rainfall of above 60 mm, a further increase in the water level is expected.” The weather bureau warned that excess floodwater would flow directly into the Tullahan River should the dam reach its overflow level. The agency said low-lying areas that may be affected include Fairview, Forest Hills Subdivision, Quirino Highway, Sta. Quiteria, and San Bartolome in Quezon City; Caloocan City; North Expressway and La Huerta Subdivision in Valenzuela City; and Malabon and Navotas. “It should also be noted that aside from the outflow from the reservoir, continuous rainfall over the watershed may further increase the river water level,” PAGASA said. Residents of the identified areas, particularly those living near riverbanks, were advised to take the necessary precautionary measures. Earlier, PAGASA said the southwest monsoon, locally known as “habagat,” continued to affect Luzon and the Visayas.

'Palong-palo': Jeepney driver in trouble over 'trip to heaven' mode, LTFRB summons PUV operator. A passenger jeepney driver is now in deep trouble for the alleged “trip to heaven” mode in a viral video wherein the uploader and the netizens pointed out the possibility of illegal substance use. “Palong-palo”, a netizen commented, referring to the alleged visible effects of illegal drugs use while the driver was plying a route on a busy road as seen in the viral video. On Saturday, the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) issued a show cause order (SCO) to the operator of the passenger jeepney to demand an explanation over what it described as disturbing content involving a public utility vehicle (PUV). Acting LTFRB Chairman Atty. Greg G. Pua, Jr. said the investigation is intended to identify the driver and set the record straight on insinuations of the netizens of the possible illegal substance use as seen in the behavior in the viral video. “This is really dangerous if the allegation is true, something that we in the LTFRB will not let pass. We assure the public that we will look into this case and part of our initial action is to ensure the driver involved will not be allowed to temporarily operate pending the result of the investigation,” said Pua. In the viral video, the driver was seen unsafe driving practices and appeared to have been unmindful of the safety and comfort of the passengers. Pua said the hearing was set on Sept. 10 to clear things up on the possibility of illegal drugs use as he noted that if the observation is true, the incident was a clear violation of the conditions set on the Certificate of Public Convenience (CPC). As operators, he said they have the obligation to ensure that the drivers they would hire are not reckless drivers and are always in good mental and physical condition since what is at stake is not only the safety of the passengers but also other road users. The viral video was monitored by the LTFRB Social Media Monitoring Team and was immediately acted upon by sending SCO to the registered operator of the passenger jeepney. Pua stressed the importance of reporting any cases or incidents of abuses and violations of public utility drivers and operators, saying the LTFRB and the public are partners in ensuring a safe and comfortable public transportation. In this case, he said the posting of the video led to the LTFRB acting on the matter. He then urged the public to report similar cases and other road safety violation involving PUVs through the LTFRB Hotline 1342, and even via social media accounts.

How a pre-game note turned prophetic for Gilas. The writing is on the wall — figuratively and literally. “Grind it – one point win.” It was written right across the whiteboard, just above all the game plans the team had prepared for weeks, inside the Gilas Pilipinas dugout before the game. Gilas head coach Tim Cone was probably the one who wrote it, never imagining that after a couple of hours, the note would look prophetic as the Nationals escaped with a thrilling 82-81 win over Jordan. Coincidental? Probably. Most likely, even. But what was clear was that note reflected the grit and fighting spirit of Gilas to take the win even if it meant with only a one-point lead. Asked about the note during the post-game press conference, Cone explained that it was simply the mentality he wants his charges to bring into the game “When you are looking for a one-point win. You want to value every possession offensively and defensively and that’s really the point of that,” said the veteran mentor. “We were not necessarily looking for a one-point win but we are trying to play as if it is going to be a one point win and that means valuing every possession offensively and defensively,” he furthered. His players eventually lived by it. Gilas trailed by as many as 18 points in the first half but came back roaring in the second and third frames before grinding it out in the fourth quarter. CJ Perez played like a man possessed in the waning minutes, slashing through the defense of Jordan to keep Gilas within striking distance. He then issued the timely assist pass — his lone for the night — to Kevin Quiambao who put Gilas in the lead, 82-79 with a big triple. Jordan came knocking when it cut the lead down to one and regained possession in the final seven seconds, only for Kai Sotto to shut the door on their comeback hopes with the game-saving block over Abdullah Olajuwon. “I would certainly prefer a 10 points win than a one point win,” said Cone with a smile. “But at this point, we just want to stay alive and keep fighting for that World Cup. We know how important it is to us, we know how important it is to the players, we know how important it is to the country,” he added

JBC opens application, nomination to post of SC Chief Justice Gesmundo who retires on Nov. 6. The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) has opened the application or nomination to the post of Supreme Court (SC) Chief Justice, who is also head of the country’s judiciary, with the compulsory retirement at age 70 of Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo on Nov. 6, 2026. The deadline for the submission of the application or nomination will be at 4:30 p.m. on October 13. Applicants or those who will submit nominations must visit the JBC website – www.jbc.judiciary.gov.ph – for the complete details and guidelines. The five most senior SC associate justices are automatically nominated to the post of Chief Justice. However, they have the option to decline the nomination. The incumbent five senior associate justices (in the order of seniority) are Marvic M.V.F. Leonen, Benjamin S. Caguioa, Ramon Paul L. Hernando, Amy C. Lazaro-Javier, and Henri Jean Paul B. Inting. However, Associate Justice Lazaro-Javier is also retiring compulsorily on Nov. 16, 2026, her 70th birthday. With her retirement, Associate Justice Rodil V. Zalameda may be considered as the fifth senior associate justice who may be automatically nominated to the Chief Justice post. Under Section 7, Article VII of the Constitution, a member of the SC – including the Chief Justice – must be a natural-born citizen, at least 40 years of age, and has served as a lower court judge or practiced law in the Philippines for 15 years or more. He or she must be a person of proven competence, integrity, probity, and independence. The JBC -- the constitutional office that accepts, screens, and nominates appointments to the judiciary, the Office of the Ombudsman and its deputies, and members of the Legal Education Board – is mandated to submit at least three nominees to President Marcos for appointment. Gesmundo was appointed SC associate justice on Aug. 14, 2017 and was promoted Chief Justice on April 5, 2021. He obtained his law degree from the Ateneo de Manila University in 1984 and passed the bar the following year. He joined the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) and was awarded Most Outstanding Solicitor in 1998. As OSG solicitor, he was also appointed commissioner of the Presidential Commission on Good Government and served the agency until Feb. 15, 2001. As assistant solicitor general, Gesmundo was appointed associate justice of the Sandiganbayan on Oct. 15, 2005. From the anti-graft court, he was promoted SC associate justice. In 2022 as Chief Justice, Gesmundo launched the five-year Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations (SPJI) to review and assess the organizational structure and operations of the various offices of the judiciary, and to develop and establish an information and communications technology infrastructure for the Philippine judiciary. The SPJI was conceived to deliver responsive and real-time justice. It is a plan anchored on four guiding principles -- timely and fair justice, transparent and accountable justice, equal and inclusive Justice, and technologically adaptive management. Since its launch four years ago, the SPJI has started to reap its three outcomes – efficiency, innovation, and access. Chief Justice Gesmundo has been conferred degree of Doctor of Laws by three universities -- Centro Escolar University School of Law and Jurisprudence on July 8, 2021, the Manuel L. Quezon University on March 26, 2022, the Philippine Christian University on August 31, 2022, and the Lyceum of the Philippines University on October 12, 2023. On Dec. 1, 2021, he was conferred the honorary rank of Knight Grand Cross of Rizal and on Sept.11, 2023, he was presented with the 2023 Chief Justice Richard W. Holmes Award of Merit by the American Judges Association, the first non-American recipient of such award. Before his government stint, Gesmundo worked as research analyst with Business Day Corporation where his articles were published by the business newspaper Business Day. He also worked as a market research officer of the Office of the Australian Trade Commissioner and as marketing officer until 1985. The son of a farmer, Juan A. Gesmundo, and public school teacher Zenaida G. Gahon, Chief Justice Gesmundo is married to Lynn Magpantay-Gesmundo with who he has a son, Alastair, and twin daughters, Ashley Nicole and Allison Arden.

Phivolcs warns of possible lahars around Pinatubo, Taal amid monsoon rains. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) on Saturday, Aug. 29, warned that continued rains brought about by the southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” may trigger lahars and muddy streamflows around Pinatubo and Taal volcanoes. Phivolcs issued the advisory after the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said monsoon rains would continue to affect western and central Luzon. “This could generate volcanic sediment flows or lahars, muddy streamflows or muddy run-off in rivers and drainage areas on Pinatubo and Taal volcanoes,” Phivolcs said. The agency urged communities in areas prone to lahars and related hazards to remain vigilant and prepared. Phivolcs said prolonged and intense rainfall may generate non-eruption lahars along major rivers draining western Pinatubo, where significant deposits from the 1991 pyroclastic density currents remain. It noted that lahars may occur along the upper and middle reaches of the Sto. Tomas-Marella and Bucao river systems and may transition into muddy streamflows and floods downstream. These may affect communities in San Marcelino, San Narciso, San Felipe, and Botolan in Zambales. “Muddy streamflows may likewise be generated along the O’Donnell and Pasig-Potrero River systems draining the Pinatubo edifice to the north and southeast, respectively and affect downstream communities in Tarlac and Pampanga Provinces,” Phivolcs said. Around Taal Volcano, prolonged and heavy rainfall may also generate muddy streamflows and runoff, particularly on the slopes west of Taal Lake, where thin deposits of remnant ash may be remobilized, the agency said. Phivolcs said muddy streamflows and runoff may recur in previously affected communities in Agoncillo and Laurel in Batangas. “DOST-PHIVOLCS strongly advises the communities and local government units of the above identified areas of risk to continually monitor the storm conditions and take pre-emptive response measures for their safety,” the agency said.

Navotas gov't tightens cybersecurity over possible threat. The Navotas City government has tightened its cybersecurity measures after receiving information about a possible threat that may affect its systems. In a statement on Saturday, Aug. 29, the city government said it is still verifying the information and has already implemented precautionary measures. The city's cybersecurity team is also closely monitoring the city’s systems to ensure that they remain secure and protected. The local government said safeguarding city data, particularly the personal information of residents, remains its top priority. It has yet to disclose the nature of the possible threat or whether any system or data has been affected. The city government said it will release verified updates when necessary and advised the public to rely only on information from its official channels.

PCSO medicine donation program augments healthcare support for PNP Quezon City. Singapore marks 61st national day. Singapore’s National Day celebration in Manila this year reflected a relationship that has become increasingly defined by the people who have built lives between the two countries. More than 150 Singaporeans and Permanent Residents based in the Philippines gathered at the Singapore Embassy on July 23 for an early celebration of Singapore’s 61st National Day, with some traveling from as far as Cebu. Singapore Minister for Foreign Affairs Dr. Vivian Balakrishnan joined the celebration, held ahead of National Day on Aug. 9. This year’s theme, “Go Beyond,” calls on Singaporeans to look beyond the country’s shores, build trusted relationships and find common purpose with others—an appropriate message for a community whose members have established careers, businesses and families in the Philippines. The occasion also comes as Singapore and the Philippines mark 57 years of diplomatic relations, established in 1969. Cooperation between the two countries now spans trade and investment, innovation, sustainability and strong people-to-people ties. Singapore Ambassador to the Philippines Constance See reflected on those connections in her National Day message published in the “Manila Bulletin” on Aug. 9. “Our relationship has been strengthened not only by agreements between governments or the investments of our companies, but also by the countless and growing connections between our people,” See wrote. Filipinos have established a significant presence in Singapore, working across healthcare, finance, technology and engineering, with many also building businesses there. Singaporeans, in turn, have made the Philippines home and developed their own professional and personal ties to the country. Economic relations remain another important pillar. According to the Philippine Statistics Authority, Singapore accounted for almost 34 percent of approved foreign investment pledges in the Philippines in 2025, amounting to ₱92.834 billion. Bilateral ties received further attention in July when President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. visited Singapore and met Prime Minister Lawrence Wong. The two leaders agreed to deepen cooperation in artificial intelligence, education and environmental sustainability. Marcos also met Singaporean business leaders amid expanding investments in data infrastructure, telecommunications and healthcare. Filipino touches The celebration also incorporated distinctly Filipino elements. The embassy unveiled “Flight,” a sculpture by Filipino artist Impy Pilapil donated by Singapore Airlines, which is marking 60 years of operations in the Philippines. Created in 2015, the sculpture was previously displayed at the airline’s SilverKris Lounge at NAIA Terminal 3 and now has a new home in the Singapore Embassy foyer. The embassy also turned to one of the Philippines’ most recognizable forms of transport for its National Day campaign: a traditional jeepney dressed in Singapore red for a special photo and video shoot celebrating the friendship between the two countries. Beyond providing a playful Filipino element to the festivities, both projects placed local creativity within Singapore’s celebration of its own national identity. The relationship also carries wider regional significance. Singapore and the Philippines have been fellow founding members of ASEAN since 1967. With the Philippines holding the ASEAN Chairmanship this year and Singapore assuming the role in 2027, the two countries will have successive opportunities to help shape the regional agenda. For the Singaporeans gathered in Manila, however, their 61st National Day was also something more personal: an opportunity to reconnect with their community and celebrate Singapore while in a country many of them now call home.

All-new Nissan Kicks e Power just launched. Nissan Philippines has just taken the wraps off the all-new Kicks e Power. The latest model offers an updated design, features designed for modern driving, and enhanced technology. First introduced in the Philippines in 2022, the Nissan Kicks brought e Power’s unique technology to the subcompact crossover segment, offering a distinct driving experience through its electric motor-driven performance. This all-new model comes four years after its market introduction, bringing enhancements together to deliver a more confident, comfortable, and connected drive, while retaining the responsive performance. Bold new exterior The all-new Kicks features a refreshed exterior design that gives the subcompact SUV a more modern and expressive look. The updated front end combines Nissan’s signature V-Motion grille with a new lighting signature with triple-arrow Daytime Running Lights for a sharper visual identity. The improved headlights that deliver wider and longer illumination, providing a clearer view of the road and enhancing visibility in low-light conditions. Behind, Nissan’s signature hexagon-shaped rear lamps give the Kicks a clean look. Interior built for everyday life Inside, the Kicks is designed to make everyday journeys more pleasant and convenient for both drivers and passengers. Nissan’s Zero Gravity seats are designed to support a comfortable seating position, while anti-heat leather upholstery helps reduce heat buildup in warm conditions. For rear passengers, an optimized seatback angle and a rear armrest contribute to a more relaxed ride, while the six-way power-adjustable driver’s seat allows drivers to find a more personalized driving position. The cabin also features a 12.3-inch Display Audio system with Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, along with NissanConnect Services with a three-year subscription, giving drivers more access to connectivity features while on the road. A smarter way to go electric At the heart of the Kicks is Nissan e POWER, delivering a 100% electric motor-driven experience with 136-PS and 280-Nm of torque. Its self-charging system uses a 1.2-liter three-cylinder gasoline engine to generate electricity for the battery, while the electric motor drives the wheels. This setup delivers the responsive feel of electric motor-driven performance, without requiring drivers to change their refueling habits. Nissan ProPILOT Advanced driver-assistance technology is also a key part of the all-new Kicks. The safety suite is called Nissan ProPILOT, designed to help reduce driving stress, particularly on highways and longer journeys. The system assists with steering, acceleration, and braking through features such as Intelligent Lane Keep Assist (LKA), which helps keep the vehicle centered in its lane, and Intelligent Cruise Control (ICC), which helps maintain a preset speed and safe distance from the vehicle ahead. In changing traffic conditions, ProPILOT can also bring the vehicle to a stop and resume driving with its Traffic Jam Assist, helping make daily commutes and long drives more convenient. The Kicks also comes with 12 additional safety and driver-assistance technologies, including: Leading Car Departure Notification (LCDN), Intelligent Forward Collision Warning (IFCW), Intelligent Forward Emergency Braking with Pedestrian Detection (IFEB), Blind Spot Warning with Blind Spot Intervention (BSW + BSI), Lane Departure Warning with Lane Departure Prevention (LDW + LDP), Rear Automatic Emergency Braking (RAEB), Tire Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS), Rear Cross Traffic Alert (RCTA), Intelligent Around View Monitor with Moving Object Detection (IAVM + MOD), High Beam Assist (HBA), and Driver Attention Alert (DAA). “The Philippines is an important market for Nissan, and we are grateful for the trust Filipino customers continue to place in our brand,” said Nissan Philippines President Yoshinori Kanazawa. “The all-new Nissan Kicks e POWER represents a new chapter for a nameplate that has become familiar to Filipino drivers. We are excited to introduce this new generation and invite customers to discover the new Nissan Kicks that are made for those who are ready to explore and Live Daring.” Availability and offers Nissan is also offering exclusive launch offers for customers looking to make the switch to electrified driving. The all-bew Kicks e Power is available in three variants: VE, ₱1,499,000; VL, ₱1,649,000; and LE Plus, ₱1,749,000 with exclusive launch offers and promo prices available until September 30, 2026. The Nissan Kicks is available in four colors: Aquamarine Metallic, Gun Metallic, Pearl White, and Moon Pearl Gray. The LE Plus is also exclusively available with a black roof. Complementing the exterior are variant-specific interior finishes, with the LE Plus featuring a new Moonstone interior combination, while the VE and VL come in classic Black. Customers can also enjoy exclusive launch offers, including a complimentary one-year Nissan Protect+ package covering prepaid maintenance with genuine Nissan oil and parts, expert servicing, and added value throughout the first year of ownership. Alongside the Kicks models on display, Kicks by Quiccs was also showcased, featuring Filipino contemporary artist Quiccs’ artistic interpretation of the nameplate. The collaboration builds on Nissan’s ongoing partnership with the artist, bringing together automotive design and Filipino creativity. Visit the Nissan Intelligent Mobility Tour from August 28 to 30 at the Glorietta Palm Drive Activity Center and explore other Nissan models through test-drive activities. Ffor those who want to be among the first to experience the all-new Nissan Kicks e Power, reservations are now open across Nissan dealerships nationwide or online at https://www.nissan.ph/reservekicks.

DSWD raises disaster response operations to Red Alert amid ‘habagat’. Amid the prolonged effects of the southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) has placed its disaster response operations on “Red Alert” in parts of Luzon and the Visayas. The agency said it heightened its alert status in compliance with National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) Memorandum No. 237, Series of 2026, which raised the national alert level from Blue to Red effective at 5 p.m. on Friday, Aug. 28, due to weather systems affecting the country. Assistant Secretary Irene Dumlao of the DSWD’s Disaster Response Management Group (DRMG) said the agency continues to gear up for the potential effects of prolonged rainfall and flooding. “Patuloy po tayong nakahanda dahil alam natin na patuloy pa rin ang epekto ng habagat sa ilang bahagi ng Luzon at Visayas (We remain prepared because we know that the southwest monsoon continues to affect parts of Luzon and the Visayas),” the DSWD spokesperson said in a statement. “Naka-heightened alert po ang ating mga Field Offices at nakahanda ang ating mga relief resources upang mabilis nating matugunan ang pangangailangan ng ating mga kababayan kung kinakailangan (Our field offices are on heightened alert, and our relief resources are ready so we can quickly respond to the needs of our fellow Filipinos, if necessary),” she added. As of 6 p.m. on Friday, Aug. 28, the DSWD had prepositioned over 3.4 million family food packs (FFPs) in warehouses and other strategic locations nationwide, based on its latest Disaster Response Operations Monitoring and Information Center (DROMIC) report. Likewise, DSWD said its Central Office (CO) has P558.77 million in Quick Response Fund (QRF) available to support immediate disaster response operations. Dumlao said DSWD field offices are closely coordinating with local government units (LGUs), particularly in areas at risk of flooding, displacement, and other disaster-related incidents, to prepare for possible relief augmentation and technical assistance. “Patuloy din po ang ating koordinasyon sa mga LGUs at iba pa nating katuwang na ahensya at LGUs upang ma-monitor natin ang sitwasyon sa mga komunidad at matiyak na mabilis ang pagresponde kung may mga pamilyang kailangan lumikas at nangangailangan ng assistance mula sa DSWD (We also continue to coordinate with local government units and our partner agencies to monitor the situation in communities and ensure a swift response should families need to evacuate and require assistance from the DSWD),” she said. As such, DSWD spokesperson reminded the public to remain vigilant and regularly monitor official weather and disaster advisories, particularly as the “habagat” continues to bring rains to affected areas. “Pinapaalalahanan po natin ang ating mga kababayan na manatiling updated sa mga opisyal na abiso ng PAGASA at ng kanilang mga lokal na pamahalaan (We remind the public to stay updated on official advisories from PAGASA and their local governments),” said Dumlao. “Hinihikayat din po natin ang lahat na agad na makipag-ugnayan sa kanilang mga LGU kung kinakailangang lumikas o kung mangangailangan ng anumang emergency assistance (We also encourage everyone to immediately coordinate with their local government units if they need to evacuate or require any emergency assistance).”
